articles.title: Why Jurgen Klopp's 'one of 83 million' cap was significant as he named two Germany squads
articles.summary: Ahead of Germany's four matches against Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (two), Jurgen Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups; "We need to rediscover the fun in all of this," said Klopp as he announced the squads
articles.body:
Ahead of the four matches against Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (two), Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups.

That list comprises 16 players who have yet to make an international appearance for Germany, including Said El Mala of Cologne, Max Rosenfelder, Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant from Freiburg and Celtic midfielder Mika Baur.

Other notable decisions include the omission of Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav, explained by Klopp as fitness-related, and his announcement that captain Joshua Kimmich will be used as a midfielder, having previously been utilised as a right-back by Julian Nagelsmann.

Nagelsmann resigned as Germany's head coach following their World Cup last-32 stage elimination by Paraguay.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen, currently on loan at Ajax from Barcelona, has been confirmed as first-choice goalkeeper, while there are recalls for Karim Adeyemi, Leeds United's Anton Stach and Brentford forward Kevin Schade.

One squad will be used for the first two games, against Netherlands in Amsterdam next Thursday, September 24, and against Greece in Augsburg three days later, on September 27.

The second group will be used for the match against Serbia in Munich on October 1 and the away trip to face Greece, in Thessaloniki on October 4.

Klopp also had a political message at his press conference, wearing a baseball cap which read "one of 83 million" in the colours of the German flag. The country is enduring a fractious political period and the far-right Alternative for Deutschland party recently achieved a significant electoral victory in Saxony-Anhalt.

In response, Klopp used his press conference to preach unity. Asked about his cap and its significance, he said: "We need to rediscover the fun in all of this. I hope I won't have to talk about political matters in the future. But I want to reclaim the flag for us. So that people feel happy and fortunate to live in this wonderful country.

"I don't want to leave national pride to the wrong people. It fills me with pride to do this job. When we spend time focused on football, it's meant to foster a sense of community and make us feel better. We have to create that atmosphere. But we also need people who embrace it."

What was the significance of Klopp's cap?

Klopp's baseball cap is going to be interpreted as a response to the state election results in Saxony-Anhalt. The far-right AfD party won over 43 per cent of the popular vote and a majority, furthering a trend for their growing support in the region and across east Germany as a whole.

But this is just the most recent issue and, in any case, the AfD cannot be described as only having prominence in the old east. Their anti-immigration, nationalistic rhetoric plays in other parts of the country, too, particularly in areas of industrial decline and that Saxony-Anhalt election result did not occur in isolation; the AfD has been polling strongly at state and federal level for several years. For many, that is a source of considerable angst and the basis for anger and division.

But there is a more general issue, too. What is the acceptable form of patriotism in Germany? What does the flag mean to different people? The legacy of national socialism makes these issues highly complicated to begin with, but as the country changes and deals with modern issues such as multiculturalism, symbols of nationalism or declarations of national pride can be interpreted in different ways or co-opted with malignant intent.

That nebulousness is a symptom of a divided nation. There are many different perspectives on what Germany is and what it should be. Not forgetting, of course, that it is a federal country to begin with, built from states with their own regional identities and, consequently, contrasting perspectives on the changing political climate.

articles.title: College football and all its craziness has finally caught up to Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: It's easy to paint Kiffin as some kind of rogue agent, but really he's simply embodying every single one of the issues that college football itself is facing...
articles.body:
There's no sport in America more chaotic, untrammeled and mesmerizing right now than college football. And there's no coach in college football more infuriating, polarizing and can't-miss than Lane Kiffin. It's like these two were made for one another.

Kiffin is college football's trickster god, a why-so-serious edgelord devoted entirely to himself, acting without shame or apology. He's neither conquering hero nor comic-book villain. He's more like a natural force, a hurricane blowing into your town delivering both national attention and instant football respectability … at substantial cost. You love him for as long as he's yours, and then one day, poof, he's gone, leaving nothing but a few motivational Instagram posts and the scent of hot-yoga candles in his wake.

This weekend, Kiffin and his current team visit the home stadium of his spurned ex. LSU-Ole Miss is getting the full-on Game of the Century treatment , from the anointment of a College GameDay telecast to the wall-to-wall coverage from every major media organization covering college football, Yahoo Sports very much included. (Hey, fish where the fish are, right?)

LSU and Ole Miss are both highly ranked programs with talented rosters and playoff potential. But let's be honest here, we're all doing the all-hands-on-deck drill because of one man. One hoodie'd, visor-wearing, smirking man who's surely enjoying every bit of the chaos he's whipping up.

Kiffin has always been this way, arriving in town with a moving truck full of promises and a playbook full of quick results, and as long as you understand this is almost surely a short-term arrangement, everything will work out just fine.

For all the grief he (justifiably) gets for his social-media persona and his casual approach to loyalty, Kiffin is a grinder, an offensive mastermind. During his brief demotion as a member of Nick Saban's Home For Wayward Former Head Coaches, Kiffin oversaw a wholesale philosophical changeover that helped Alabama get faster and more aerial; the result was another few years of the Saban Dynasty.

(Kiffin wouldn't see all of that dynasty unfold, of course; his other trait — an unerring ability to piss off his employers — would get him kicked to the curb in Tuscaloosa during the 2016-season playoffs. His replacement at Alabama? Steve Sarkisian. College football time is a flat circle.)

Now at LSU, and with NIL in full effect, Kiffin has resources far beyond any he could access at any previous stop, a massive war chest backed by the state's governor. That's allowed him to build a team that — while not yet truly tested this season — sure as hell looks ready to go toe-to-toe with the nation's best. But even that isn't enough for Kiffin, who's jeopardized his entire institution's standing by insisting, past the point of all reason, that he wanted to bring back players who had worked out with NFL teams.

The NFL-players-in-college story is a done-and-dusted issue now, but why did Kiffin push it so far? Simple: because he was told he couldn't. The value of the players to LSU's roster is debatable; the value of trolling the entire college football universe is inestimable. You don't declare "Imagine if we had pro players" at halftime of a tiger-skinning without knowing exactly how that's going to land the next morning all over social media.

Now, it's easy to paint Kiffin as some kind of rogue or rebel, flaunting the rules of college football for his own gain. But widen the lens a bit. Kiffin is simply embodying every single one of the issues that college football itself is facing — and causing — every single day. What are conferences, broadcast networks and portal-hopping players doing, after all, but imitating Kiffin's what's-in-it-for-me ethos?

So much of college football existed for so many years on a sort of unspoken-agreement basis that, until the last few years, the sport didn't reckon with the possibility that people like Kiffin would just … do what they want. Jumping from a program in the midst of its most successful season ever, trying to lure players and coaches along with you, looking to bring back players who had already gone pro … college football fans tend to forget that the sport is governed, when it's governed at all, by rules, not laws, and you know what they say about how rules are made.

Yes, Kiffin leaves pretty much every job under a cloud of rage and controversy … just like the programs leaping from one conference to another, disrupting decades of tradition. Sure, Kiffin exhibits zero institutional loyalty, not unlike the players (and their agents) engineering jaunt after portal jaunt. Kiffin positions himself as a rebel and an outlaw and "hated," knowing it'll bring in eyeballs … just like the Pat McAfee-led College GameDay.

Kiffin knows that we're in a world where the old rules of decorum don't apply, where you grab what you can with both hands and dare people to stop you. He's the most obvious example of that, but he's by no means the only one. For every broadcaster sanctimoniously criticizing Kiffin, there's a media outlet thanking heaven he's bringing in eyeballs.

Lane Kiffin is the most fascinating figure in college football right now, but he's not an aberration or an outlier. He's just been hanging out waiting for the sport to catch up with him … and in 2026, it surely has.

articles.title: 'Make our fans proud': Dani Ramirez eyes win as East Bengal target Al-Shorta after historic ACL Two draw

articles.body: KOLKATA: East Bengal’s Spanish attacker Dani Ramirez believes that his team’s stunning 2-2 draw at Jordanian champions Al Hussein SC will help them grow in confidence in Asia’s second-tier club football.Ramirez scored one and provided assist to Anwar Ali’s goal as Antonio Lopez Habas’ team became the first Indian club to register a point in an away game in the rebranded AFC Champions League Two. It could’ve been more remarkable for them had they not conceded a goal at the death to let their 2-0 lead slip away.Ramirez, however, insisted after the match in Amman that they would go for a win when they host Iraq’s Al-Shorta in their next match at the Salt Lake Stadium on Oct 13."I hope we can win our second ACL Two group match against Iraq's Al-Shorta on 13 October in Kolkata, and make our fans proud.“We still need to improve in a few areas, and that introspection started in the dressing room right after the match. That said, this performance will give us a huge confidence boost, and we will carry these lessons into the next match,” Ramirez told the club’s media team.Only three foreigners, playmaker Mohammed Rashid and Croatian defender and debutant Diego Zivulic being the other two, were available for East Bengal ACL2 Group D opener. But they are likely to face Al-Shorta at home with the possibility of three more foreign attackers —Australia’s Chris Ikonomidis, Ivory Coast’s Ake Arnaud Loba and Polish striker Lukasz Zwoliński, being available for selection.“We played well as a unit (in Amman), and with our fans backing us at home, I am confident we can deliver a positive result,” Ramirez maintained.Al-Shorta are leading the Group D after the first-round action, following their 1-0 win over Oman’s Al Seeb.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Things not looking good as India's elite men suffer three draws at Samarkand Olympiad; women beat Finland
articles.summary: Chess News: Things are not looking too good for defending champions India at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.No. 52 seeds Indonesia held their own aga.
articles.body: Things are not looking too good for defending champions India at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.No. 52 seeds Indonesia held their own against the second seeds and eked out three draws, losing a game to only Nihal Sarin and went down by the smallest of margins (1.5-2.5) in the second round on Thursday.India’s celebrated elite men players, who largely play among fellow 2600-plus players and hence get rating protection even if they play out draws, seem to be found wanting in a street fight - an essence of sport where a fancied player has more at stake than the underdog. Therein lies the charm of the Swiss League and Olympiad.Nihal won with white pieces against Abdul Hafiz, a player about Elo 250 lower than him. R Praggnanandhaa, D Gukesh and Vidit Gujrathi could only draw with players about Elo 300 lower than them.India had rested Arjun Erigaisi after he lost in the opener and hence world champion Gukesh was promoted from the designated fourth board to the third on the second successive day.Pragg took the top board but could not breach the defence of Susanto Megaranto after five and a half hours and 79 moves.The top seeded India women’s team defeated Finland 3.5-0.5 with reasonable conviction but R Vaishali could not win on the top board and Divya Deshmukh flirted with danger before getting a semi-gift.Koneru Humpy was rested. Women’s 48th seeds Montenegro held second seeds Georgia 2-2.If top seed USA’s Levon Aronian’s creative risk-taking was punished with a draw in the opening round, his 23-year-old teammate Awonder Liang suffered defeat against IM Khuyagtsogt Itgelt of Mongolia in the second round.Former world champion Ding Liren, who is given the top board by China despite his recent troubles, messed up a sumptuous winning position with plenty of time in hand against Chile’s Rodrigo Vasquez Schroeder, and managing only half a point.Pakistan, who forfeited against Israel in the opener, presumably in protest against the conflict in Palestine, blanked Seychelles 4-0.Inclusivity is one of the stronger points at the Olympiad. The third edition of the Olympiad for People with Disabilities was held at the same venue.These players were given an extra half an hour each for each of the seven rounds to complete their games. Poland regained the gold that they had won in the inaugural edition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Maradona tuvo responsabilidad en su propia muerte
articles.standfirst: El perito José Antonio Maya declaró en el juicio que "Maradona se murió de golpe y no hubo alternativa. No es culpa de Maradona, es responsabilidad de Maradona"
articles.summary: El perito José Antonio Maya declaró en el juicio que "Maradona se murió de golpe y no hubo alternativa. No es culpa de Maradona, es responsabilidad de Maradona"
articles.body: José Antonio Maya, médico clínico y perito de Lepoldo Luque, principal acusado de la muerte de Diego Armando Maradona, dijo en el juicio que los signos de alarma que podrían haberse detectado antes del fallecimiento requerían que el astro fuera revisado, pero no se dejó: "Es responsabilidad de Maradona". "Maradona se murió de golpe y no hubo alternativa. Las cosas que podían haberse detectado exigían mínimamente que el médico pudiera verlo. Lo que pudo haberse manifestado ahí es el principio de autonomía. No es culpa de Maradona, es responsabilidad de Maradona", dijo Maya. El principio de autonomía en salud es el derecho de toda persona a decidir de forma libre, voluntaria e informada sobre su propio cuerpo y los tratamientos médicos que recibe. Ha sido documentado que el 18 de noviembre de 2020, una semana antes de la muerte, el exfutbolista echó a su médico de cabecera, Leopoldo Luque, y también al médico clínico contratado por Swiss Medical, Pedro Di Spagna, y al nutricionista Luciano Spena. A lo largo del juicio numerosos testigos describieron al astro como "un paciente difícil". El galeno clínico Di Spagna, acusado en el juicio, concurrió al domicilio luego de que un enfermero le comunicara que Maradona tenía una de las piernas edematizadas. Sin embargo, Maradona se negó a recibirlo. "Pienso que cuando Maradona se sintió enfermo permitió que los médicos actuaran y acá se sentía lo suficientemente bien para no darle oportunidad a un médico para que actúe", agregó el perito. Al igual que el testigo que declaró más temprano, el cardiólogo Ricardo Iglesias, Maya negó que Maradona fuera un paciente con riesgo cardíaco o que tuviera alguna patología del corazón. "En el 2000 dijeron que la cocaína había producido una miocardiopatía irrecuperable, pero en el 2007 dijeron que su corazón estaba sano", matizó Maya. El médico dijo que la miocardiopatía dilatada es una enfermedad que produce adelgazamiento de las paredes del corazón y no era el caso de Maradona, pues esas paredes estaban engrosadas, según determinó la policía científica. Maya participó en la junta médica interdisciplinaria creada en 2021 para analizar las circunstancias de la muerte del astro. La junta concluyó que el accionar de los médicos fue "inadecuado, deficiente y temerario", y que los médicos ignoraron los signos de alarma que presentó el paciente, en un informe que Maya firmó en disconformidad, al tiempo que consignó un documento propio. En su interrogatorio, el fiscal Patricio Ferrari citó un fragmento del informe consignado por Maya, que indicaba que el edema que Maradona tenía en el tronco "es el único signo que debieron advertir los médicos y orientar medidas o reinternación, en caso de poder examinarlo". "Los edemas pueden no significar un signo de alarma, sí una advertencia de que hay algo para revisar", dijo el testigo este jueves. Ante la consulta sobre si es de buena práctica médica no hacer nada durante varios días ante tal advertencia, Maya insistió: "Durante varios días no, pero se tiene que dejar revisar".

articles.title: Craig Bellamy: Wales boss was right to speak to Burnley - David Adams
articles.summary: FAW chief football officer David Adams says he has a list of potential replacements for when Craig Bellamy ends his spell as Wales head coach.
articles.body:
Football Association of Wales (FAW) chief football officer David Adams says Craig Bellamy was right to hold talks with Burnley in the summer.

Wales boss Bellamy - whose contract with the FAW expires after Euro 2028 - has made no secret of his desire to manage at club level in the future.

He spoke with former club Burnley in the summer over the possibility of being named as Scott Parker's successor at Turf Moor.

However, Bellamy remained with Wales and has since stated it was his decision to stay in his role with the national team.

Despite the saga, Adams believes it was the correct decision for Bellamy to speak with the Clarets.

"The way it played out was unfortunate, things get leaked these days," he told the latest episode of BBC's Feast of Football podcast, which can only be found on BBC Sounds.

"Naturally, the longer things go on, people start to make their own noise in some respects.

"Internally, Craig has always been very open and transparent about opportunities.

"We all know that Craig wants to eventually go and work in club football, he's made that very clear across his time here.

"For him to go and speak to Burnley was the right thing to do, knowing that he does want to do that at some point."

Adams held regular talks with Burnley chairman Alan Pace in the summer, as he did during the process that led to Bellamy leaving the Lancashire club in 2024 to take charge of Wales.

"We were happy for Craig to go and speak to them," he added. "And then unfortunately, the way it played out was that they were saying he had accepted the job when he hadn't.

"Craig was telling us the same thing as that and then one morning he rang and said 'I'm staying'.

"Craig's very transparent, we speak a lot, we get on well, so that's how it landed really."

Amid concerns over the possibility of losing Bellamy, Adams revealed he continues to assess future managerial candidates as part of the FAW's succession planning process.

"Behind the scenes in my job, I have to be alert to these things and I have to have a list of people in the background that I'd speak to if [Bellamy's departure] ever materialised," he added.

"We've got a profile of what we're looking for, which we've been pretty successful in doing by selecting former international players into the role.

"That's always our preference, to find someone who is connected to Wales, is passionate about Wales and has Wales in their heart.

"That's been a really good profile of manager to look at in the last 10 years and we would try and stick to that profile ideally."

Does Bellamy need to win back Wales fans?

Wrexham's Broadhead to miss Wales games with injury

Adams described the news that Cardiff's Principality Stadium will host the women's Champions League final in 2029 as a "game-changer" for the nation.

Cardiff City Stadium hosted the event in 2017 in the same year the men's final was played at Principality Stadium - known as National Stadium of Wales for Uefa events due to sponsorship rules.

"It's absolutely incredible, a game-changer for us," he said.

"You've seen the growth in the women's game. When I first came into the job, we were getting maybe 1,000 people at Rodney Parade for women's games.

"We got 15,000 at Cardiff City Stadium in this last campaign, so you can see the growth and how quickly the game is moving."

Adams says young females seeing role models play at the home of Cardiff City and Principality Stadium is "just inspirational for those players".

Wales' women's side qualified for a major tournament for the first time under Rhian Wilkinson as they reached Euro 2025 in Switzerland.

They are now aiming to secure a spot at a World Cup for the first time and continue their 2027 qualification bid with a double header against Albania in October.

Further down the line, the 2035 women's World Cup will be held in the United Kingdom, with England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales all due to host matches for the global showpiece.

With Wales bidding to qualify and be competitive at the tournament in future, FAW chiefs remain determined to strengthen their player pool.

Despite the huge progress made in recent years, Adams feels the governing body still has plenty of work to do.

"Our goal is to create a pathway, which hasn't been there for women's football, where girls can actually play in a talent system which prepares them to play in tournament football on a consistent basis," he said.

"I don't think we're there yet, personally. I think what we've done in the last three years is fantastic, with the girls' regional programme.

"But now we've got to try and make sure the girls graduate out of that system and play in the top leagues across Europe.

"That's what gives you the best chance of qualifying consistently for major tournaments."

articles.title: Deion Sanders Says He 'Made Some Calls' to Jimmy Horn Jr. Before WR's Browns Contract
articles.summary: After one of his former players got cut this week, Colorado head coach Deion Sanders attempted to help Jimmy Horn Jr. find his next team.
articles.body:
After one of his former players got cut this week, Colorado head coach Deion Sanders attempted to help Jimmy Horn Jr. find his next team.

The Buffaloes' head coach said on his weekly coaches show that he quickly called Horn after he was waived by the Carolina Panthers this week. Horn has since signed with the Cleveland Browns, where Sanders' son, Shedeur, is the backup quarterback.

"I made some calls to him. Immediately," Sanders (36:40 mark). "Jimmy's great."

Horn spent two seasons playing for Sanders and Colorado, recording 441 yards and a touchdown in his final campaign with the Buffaloes. He was a sixth-round draft pick by the Panthers in 2025, recording 11 receptions for 108 yards in 13 games as a rookie.

Sanders and Colorado are off to a 2-0 start after a season-opening win over Georgia Tech and a victory over Weber State last week. The Buffs will look to stay undefeated this week as they face Northwestern on Saturday.

articles.summary: MARCA entrevista en Múnich al ariete inglés del Bayern, otro de los candidatos al premio
articles.body: Harry Edward Kane (1993, Londres) nos recibe en una sala del Allianz Arena de Múnich a eso de las 23.50 de la noche, tras jugar un partido. Harry es muy profesional, en todos los sentidos. También en su compromiso de atender a MARCA sea la hora que sea, con fotos especiales incluidas. HK posa con la simpatía de un señor del fútbol. Pregunta. Empecemos hablando de la Champions. Lo ha ganado todo a nivel alemán, y por eso, la Champions parece su mayor desafío con el Bayern. Respuesta: Sí, así es. La pasada edición fue realmente buena para nosotros: segundos en la Fase Liga, con siete victorias y una derrota. Y luego tuvimos partidos muy buenos: Atalanta, Real Madrid... Ése fue muy especial, y ante el PSG, claro. Dos partidos increíbles para los aficionados. Nuestra ajustada derrota fue dura de asimilar. Estuvimos muy cerca, teníamos la confianza y calidad necesarias para estar en la final. Pero esto es la Champions: todo se decide por márgenes muy pequeños. R. ¿ Y este año? R. Se trata de hacer más o menos lo mismo, y conquistar ese último paso. Este Bayern tiene el hambre necesaria como grupo, como equipo, y también el entrenador correcto. P. La final será en Madrid, y en la Fase Liga tendrán que enfrentarse al Atlético. R. Sí. Y creo que nunca he jugado contra ellos, será mi primera vez. El Atleti ha demostrado lo buenos que pueden ser. Llegaron a semis la pasada Champions, y tienen todo mi respeto: será un partido difícil pero estaremos preparados. En ese estadio (Metropolitano) perdí una final de Champions (con el Tottenham) y fue un momento duro. Espero regresar y tener una historia diferente. . P. Usted es un caso inusual: a más edad, más goles marca. ¿Cuál es su secreto? R. Uno de ellos lo conocen ustedes bien [Harry se refiere a su doctor deportivo personal, el madrileño Alejandro Elorriaga]. Alejandro ha desempeñado un papel muy importante en mi éxito. P. ¿Qué le ha dado desde que está con él hace unos años? R. Alejandro desempeña un papel fundamental en mi actual estado. Trabajamos mucho en la sombra. Llevamos ya seis años y medio juntos [desde marzo de 2020] y él es una de las principales razones por las que puedo rendir a este nivel y disputar tantos partidos. No es casualidad que haya seguido mejorando estos años, ya que, como algunos creen, a esta edad el rendimiento suele decaer. Pero en mi caso ha ocurrido casi lo contrario. El trabajo que realizamos con Alejandro resulta sumamente gratificante y satisfactorio para ambos. Es, además, una gran persona y pasamos mucho tiempo juntos, así que, naturalmente, quiero agradecerle enormemente toda su labor. P. ¿Y qué más secretos tiene? R. El fútbol a veces tiene que ver con el momento, y estar en el Bayern, con el gran equipo que tengo a mi lado, me permite marcar muchos goles y participar, además, en el juego, pasar, defender y todo lo que disfruto para ayudar al equipo. Honestamente, me siento tan bien física y mentalmente... ¡como nunca! Tengo que aprovechar este momento al máximo porque cuando te haces mayor, el tiempo no dura para siempre. Pero ahora estoy en un momento realmente bueno. P. ¿No se cansa de celebrar goles? R. Nunca. Marcar es la mejor sensación posible. Es una descarga de adrenalina increíble. También hay una sensación de alivio enorme. Es una sensación que sé que echaré de menos cuando deje de jugar. P. Es uno de los candidatos al Balón de Oro. Sé que no le gusta hablar de sus méritos, pero 73 goles en 65 partidos (entre Bayern e Inglaterra en la 25-26)... podrían merecer premio. R. Es complicado. Nunca me ha gustado hablar demasiado de mí mismo. Lo único que diría es que la temporada pasada fue increíble, a nivel personal y de equipo. Fue, por mucho, la mejor temporada de mi vida. Es verdad que llegar a 73 goles, la segunda cifra más alta de la historia [tras los 82 en 69 en la 11-12 de Leo Messi] habla por sí sola. Estoy extremadamente orgulloso de ello. Sólo puedo agradecer a mis compañeros y a todos los que me ayudaron a que fuera posible. Pero el Balón de Oro no está en mis manos. Depende de las personas que votan. Desde mi punto de vista, la temporada pasada ya es pasado. Ahora estoy centrado en esta y tengo ganas de ver qué más puedo hacer. Sé que se va a hablar mucho del Balón hasta octubre, porque es un gran premio. P. Hay una curiosidad, Harry. Esta edición 2026 es, por primera vez, en Londres. ¿Qué le sugiere eso? R. Sí, mucha gente me lo ha dicho y quizá sea un buen presagio. Por supuesto, que sea en mi ciudad natal lo haría todavía más especial. Así que sí, es una sensación extraña que se celebre allí este año. Tendremos que esperar y ver qué pasa. P. Siempre le da méritos a sus compañeros. Lo hizo ya al recibir la Bota de Oro [premio al mejor goleador de las Ligas europeas]. Si consigue una tercera Bota, lo colocaría en el podio histórico junto a Messi [seis] y Cristiano [cuatro]. Nadie, fuera de ellos dos, ha ganado tres. R. Messi y Ronaldo [Cristiano] dominaron el fútbol durante toda una generación. Son dos de los mejores de la historia. Formar parte de esa conversación, ya es algo especial. Es un objetivo. Como delantero, se espera de mí que marque goles. La Bota de Oro no es mi único objetivo, pero, por supuesto, sé que, si la gano, también estaré ayudando al equipo. Así que todo eso simplemente me motiva. Cada vez que gano una, quiero otra, y después otra, y esta vez no será diferente. Espero estar ahí otra vez esta temporada, marcando tantos goles como pueda en la Bundesliga, y veremos si puedo conseguir otra. P. Con Messi, por cierto, coincidió en un duelo polémico en el Mundial. Aquel Inglaterra-Argentina de semis. Pero, al acabar, tuvieron enorme respeto usted y Leo. El uno para el otro. ¿Cómo recuerda aquello? R. Obviamente, para mí fue duro aquel día. Un momento difícil al quedar eliminados de esa manera. Pero tengo muchísimo respeto por Messi. Lo vi crecer como futbolista. Creo que es simplemente un jugador increíble y también una persona increíble, por lo que me cuentan las personas que lo conocen. Lo he tratado sólo un par de veces, pero me parece una persona muy humilde. Siempre ha puesto al equipo por delante de él, y creo que ésa es una de las razones por las que Argentina tuvo el éxito que tuvo. De aquel día, recuerdo que lo abracé y le deseé buena suerte para la final. No fue nuestro Mundial al final, pero de eso se trata un Mundial: los mejores jugadores enfrentándose en el escenario más grande y, por supuesto, siempre va a haber un perdedor. Aquel día, tras perder, intenté mantener la cabeza alta y mostrar respeto por el otro equipo. Creo que eso fue algo importante, y especialmente hacia Leo por lo increíble que ha sido durante tantos años en el fútbol. P. Viniendo de Madrid, debo preguntarle por José Mourinho, su antiguo entrenador en el Tottenham. ¿Fue alguien 'special' para usted? R. Sí, adoro a José. Tuvimos una relación realmente buena en el Tottenham. No terminó de la manera que queríamos y que José no tuviera la oportunidad de dirigir aquella final [HK se refiere a la final de la Carabao Cup 20-21, pues Mou fue destituido en abril] fue duro. También fue difícil para mí. Pero sí, tuve una relación muy buena con él. Jugué algunos de mis mejores partidos en el Tottenham durante su etapa. Gané la Bota de Oro y también el premio al máximo asistente en el mismo año. Me dio mucha libertad para ser yo mismo, para jugar y para bajar a recibir. Y creo que, como persona, es alguien que entiende cada detalle del juego, ya sea con balón, sin balón, en lo táctico, con el árbitro… sea lo que sea, entiende cada situación. Le tengo mucho respeto. Es verdad que no nos hemos visto mucho desde que dejó el Tottenham, pero quizá este año nos enfrentemos en la Champions y será bueno poder reencontrarme con él. P. ¿Diría que, con José, el Real Madrid es todavía un rival más difícil para el Bayern? R. El Real ha fichado buenos jugadores y Mou es un gran entrenador que sacará lo mejor de los jugadores que tiene. El Madrid siempre tiene algunos de los mejores jugadores del mundo, y este año no es diferente, igual que el anterior. Sabemos que hay muchas posibilidades de que nos enfrentemos a ellos más adelante en la competición. El Madrid, en la Champions, siempre va a estar ahí, en las últimas rondas. Nosotros estuvimos por encima de ellos el año pasado [les eliminaron en cuartos de final], pero también sabemos que fue un partido muy difícil. Y con José ahora será todavía más complicado. P. Jude Bellingham ha empezado bien la temporada. ¿Cómo lo ve? R. Jude y yo tuvimos una conexión muy buena en el Mundial, por la manera en la que jugábamos y nos pasábamos el balón. Gran conexión con y sin balón. Y también fuera del campo construimos una relación realmente fuerte, y eso sólo puede ayudar a la Selección. Es genial ver cómo se ha adaptado tan bien a Madrid. Hablé un poco con él durante el Mundial sobre José Mourinho, y sabía que le iba a encantar Mourinho. Y sabía que José adoraría a Jude, y obviamente parece que ya tienen una buena relación. Jude ha empezado genial. Y desde el punto de vista de Inglaterra, es fantástico ver eso. P. Ahora está feliz en Múnich, pero... ¿pudo haber jugado alguna vez en LaLiga en el pasado? R. Hubo momentos que sí. No diría que oportunidades claras, pero sí hubo algunas conversaciones en el pasado. Respeto mucho LaLiga. El Barcelona, el Madrid y el Atlético son algunos de los clubes más grandes del mundo. Yo crecí viendo a Ronaldo, a Messi… Tengo muchísimo respeto por esos equipos. Ya sabemos: en el fútbol puede pasar cualquier cosa. Nunca descarto nada, pero por ahora, como he dicho antes, estoy extremadamente feliz en Alemania. P. En unos días. la segunda estrella de España debutará en Wembley ante Inglaterra en la Nations League. ¿Cómo ve ese partido? R. Difícil. España es la actual campeona de Europa y campeona del mundo. Nosotros hemos estado muy cerca durante estos últimos años de ellos, pero España ha sido el equipo que ha conseguido llegar hasta el final, y nosotros, no. Los respetamos mucho. Pero también es una oportunidad para nosotros de empezar bien esta Nations League. España la ganó hace un par de años y eso les ayudó luego a alcanzar el nivel en el que están ahora. Y para Inglaterra es un espejo. No hemos ganado un trofeo desde hace muchísimo tiempo y quizá este año, con la Nations, podamos hacerlo. Eso podría ayudarnos de cara a la Eurocopa 2028, que se jugará en casa. Pero sí, contra España será un partido difícil por la manera en la que mantienen el balón, los jugadores que tienen Tengo muchas ganas de jugar ese choque. P. Voy a acabar hablando de su familia. Una esposa que conoce desde la adolescencia, cuatro hijos...¿Es uno de los secretos de su carrera? R. Creo que sí. Creo que no se habla suficientemente de lo importante que es la estabilidad familiar en el fútbol profesional, especialmente cuando hablamos de jugadores jóvenes. Y es muy importante. Es verdad que yo he tenido muchísima suerte de haber encontrado a mi mujer, con la que hasta fui al colegio, y de tener aquí a mis padres, a mi hermano y a mis suegros. Sé que no siempre es así para todo el mundo, porque cada persona tiene una situación diferente. Pero creo que cuando eres feliz fuera del campo, cuando estás asentado y la vida va bien, eso se traslada a estar feliz dentro. Así que yo estoy extremadamente agradecido por todo lo que ellos hacen por mí y por el apoyo que me dan. Todo lo que hago intento hacerlo como equipo y con ellos. Son mi mayor apoyo.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal revive con Valdano su incidente racista en el Bernabéu: "Que me llame negro no me va a molestar, soy negro"
articles.standfirst: "He sentido el racismo 1.000 veces. La gente indirectamente es racista contigo pero no se dan cuenta"
articles.summary: "He sentido el racismo 1.000 veces. La gente indirectamente es racista contigo pero no se dan cuenta"
articles.body: Movistar Plus Deportes ha ofrecido otro adelanto de la entrevista a Lamine Yamal que emitirá el programa 'Universo Valdano' el viernes 18 a las 21:00 h. En este segundo extracto de la charla Jorge Valdano habla con el delantero del F.C. Barcelona sobre si vive racismo en España, y el joven futbolista revive un episodio racista que sufrió en el Santiago Bernabéu jugando con el Real Madrid. "¿Has sentido el racismo de una manera, digámosle, directa?", le pregunta Valdano campeón del Mundial con España y serio candidato a ganar el Balón de Oro. La respuesta de Lamine Yamal fue contundente: "Sí, 1.000 veces". "La gente indirectamente es racista contigo, pero a lo mejor no se dan cuenta. Muchos comentarios, muchas miradas... son racistas y no se dan cuenta", explicó. El genio de Rocafonda, barrio de Mataró (Barcelona) en el que se crio, subrayó que "también yo he salido de un sitio en el que no es que esté asumido, porque lo que está mal nunca se puede asumir, pero no te molesta". Lamine Yamal puso como ejemplo del racismo que ha sufrido en España el comportamiento de un sector del Santiago Bernabéu durante un Clásico contra el Real Madrid. "Por ejemplo, el típico vídeo que salió del Santiago Bernabéu en el que nos decían de todo a mí y a Raphinha y la gente se sorprendía de mi reacción. Al final que esa persona me llame negro no me va a molestar en nada, soy negro, no soy de ningún color, otra cosa es que esté bien o esté mal porque me lo dice de forma despectiva. Está mal, pero lo que no voy a hacer yo, que estoy jugando un partido, donde él (el espectador) ha pagado la entrada para verme, es enfadarme por una persona que me ha faltado al respeto", compartió. En octubre de 2024 se escucharon Insultos racistas a Lamine Yamal tras marcar en el Bernabéu: "¡Puto negro!", "¡Puto Moro!", "¡Tu puta madre!" o "¡Mena de mierda!". Meses después LaLiga, que denunció los hechos ante la Policía Nacional, prohibió la entrada a los estadios durante un año y 30 horas de tareas socioeducativas al menor que insultó a Lamine Yamal en el Clásico. "Con esta actuación, LaLiga reitera su compromiso firme en la lucha contra el racismo y cualquier manifestación de odio en el fútbol", declaró Javier Tebas. En un primer extracto de la entrevista Lamine Yamal le dijo a Jorge Valdano una frase que ha dado la vuelta al mundo: "Creo que me merezco el Balón de Oro por lo que he ganado". "¿A quién se lo daría yo? Al mejor jugador del mundo. ¿A quién se lo van a dar? Eso ya es una conversación muy larga... Yo creo, sinceramente, que los mejores del mundo somos dos y este año me lo merecería yo por lo que he ganado. Para mí, somos Mbappé y yo los dos mejores del mundo. Para mí está claro y todo el mundo que ve los partidos lo sabe", explicó el delantero español.

articles.title: Junior es una realidad
articles.standfirst: El central del Girona, con 17 años recién cumplidos, enlaza cinco titularidades y ante el Castellón se estrenó como goleador
articles.summary: El central del Girona, con 17 años recién cumplidos, enlaza cinco titularidades y ante el Castellón se estrenó como goleador
articles.body: Hay talentos que salen cada cierto tiempo. Pasa en el Girona y en otros tantos clubes. Talentos cada vez más jóvenes que sacan la cabeza en categorías inferiores y tienen la suerte de tener un entrenador que cree en él sin mirar el DNI ni el el contexto de presión que tiene un proyecto como el del club catalán, que pasa por volver a Primera cuanto antes. Holmes Junior es de esos futbolistas al que sólo con pocos minutos se le ve una calidad innata y una pose de jugador hecho y derecho. Nacido en Reus el agosto del 2009, Junior sorprendió con tan sólo 16 años durante la pretemporada a las órdenes de Quique Álvarez, que vio en él un jugador diferente y le dio minutos para mostrarse, también obligado por las circunstancias y la falta de efectivos en el eje de la defensa. Con el inicio de la competición, al técnico no le tembló la mano y tampoco se decantó por hacer experimentos para seguir apostando por el central con pasado en las categorías inferiores del Real Madrid, el Nàstic de Tarragona y, desde el 2025, del Girona. Lejos de ver temblar sus piernas ante atacantes imponentes y mucho más veteranos, Junior ha dado un paso adelante que le ha permitido disputar como titular los cinco primeros encuentros, ganarse una renovación de contrato acorde a su rendimiento (hasta el 2029) y, en el último encuentro contra el Castellón, estrenarse como goleador. Increíble. "Desde que llegó en pretemporada, ha demostrado querer aprender y tener actitud para mejorar cada día. A nivel competitivo y de maduración está por encima de la media de su edad y estamos encantados con él. Junior es una sorpresa, pero cada día que pasa lo deja de ser para convertirse en una realidad", dijo Quique Álvarez después de la derrota de su equipo contra el Castellón. Holmes Junior, que tenía que volver al filial para competir en Segunda RFEF, se atreve a mandar a los compañeros, va al corte con potencia cuando la acción lo requiere y celebra con su afición las entradas y recuperaciones con éxito ante cualquier rival, al que reta y encara como un veterano sin miedo a nada. El ADN de Junior es así y ahora mismo, no parece que Mumin, teórico titular pero también lejos de su mejor nivel de forma, pueda sacarlo del once. La temporada es muy larga, pero ahora mismo el central apunta alto. El futbolista del 2009 tiene doble nacionalidad española y colombiana por ascendencia y es un fijo en las categorías inferiores de la selección española, la que eligió ante la posibilidad de jugar con los cafeteros, que no se darán por vencidos y volverán a la carga para convencer al jugador y su entorno. El pasado verano, el central disputó el Europeo sub 17 con España, ayudando a los compañeros a alcanzar las semifinales. Ahora, Junior ha sido convocado por la sub-18 española y se perderá los partidos ligueros ante el Albacete y Mallorca. Quizás la próxima cita será para apuntar más alto de lo que su edad refleja.

articles.title: Espanyol - Elche | El colista examina las dudas pericas: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: El cuadro perico busca la regularidad ante unos ilicitanos que esperan estirar las buenas sensaciones mostradas ante el Madrid
articles.summary: El cuadro perico busca la regularidad ante unos ilicitanos que esperan estirar las buenas sensaciones mostradas ante el Madrid
articles.body: El Espanyol recibe al Elche en su feudo con la firme obligación de despejar dudas y reencontrarse con la victoria. Tras completar una semana gris marcada por la irregularidad, en la que cosechó un triunfo y una derrota sin desplegar su mejor fútbol, la escuadra blanquiazul necesita dar un golpe sobre la mesa ante su afición para rearmar su confianza. Enfrente estará un conjunto ilicitano sumido en una situación crítica: colista en solitario y sin margen de error, pero esperando tras apretar al Madrid. El Espanyol recibe esta noche al Elche en el RCDE Stadium. Los de Manolo González quieren sumar tres puntos que se antojan importantes. Tras la derrota ante el Rayo Vallecano a domicilio, el equipo perico quiere sumar un nuevo triunfo ante su gente para recuperar las buenas sensaciones, llegar bien al parón liguero y lograr la segunda victoria del curso como en su estadio, donde los de Manolo González deben hacerse fuertes para perseguir los objetivos marcados. En una semana cargada de partidos y después de dos encuentros consecutivos jugando como visitante ante Osasuna y Rayo Vallecano, el Espanyol vuelve a jugar ante su gente, donde ha mostrado su mejor cara y donde el apoyo de su afición es siempre fundamental. Para el duelo de esta noche, Manolo González no podrá contar con Omar El Hilali, que vio la cartulina roja en el encuentro del pasado martes disputado en Butarque. El técnico perico tendrá que buscar una solución para suplir al lateral diestro. Veremos si, además, debido a la acumulación de minutos, Manolo González opta por más cambios y regresa al once tipo que mejores resultados le ha dado este curso. Destacar que, por primera vez, Gorosabel entrará en la convocatoria blanquiazul y podría debutar con el Espanyol. El Elche visita al Espanyol con sus primeras urgencias de la temporada. Necesita ganar para evitar irse al largo parón hundido y sin victorias. Sólo ha sumado 2 puntos de 18 y ha encajado 16 goles, con el guardameta Dituro como señalado. Como clavos a los que agarrarse, viene de igualar un 0-2 ante el Real Madrid (2-3), aunque encajó en el añadido su tercera derrota en tres partidos como local. Y ha sumado en dos de sus tres salidas, ante Dépor (1-1) y la última en Bilbao (1-1). El cambio de sistema de Anselmi, pasando de tres centrales y dos carrileros a cuatro atrás, ha dado más sobriedad al entramado defensivo. Y apunta a tener continuidad en Barcelona. Eso sí, el técnico franjiverde realizará algunas modificaciones para refrescar el once, tras el enorme desgaste del martes. Queda la duda de si apostará por uno o dos puntas. Incluso si habrá o no cambio en la portería. La racha contra el momento. Roberto Fernández llega afianzado como la principal referencia en el ataque del Espanyol tras disputar 523 minutos repartidos en 6 encuentros, en los que ha firmado una notable efectividad de cara a puerta con 6 goles y 6 disparos entre los tres palos. Enfrente está Osorio con tan solo 146 minutos acumulados en 3 partidos y una diana que hizo temblar a todo un Madrid. Hoy, con mucho en juego, ambos delanteros tienen que confirmar que su instinto sigue intacto.

articles.title: Árbitro madrileño en el derbi madrileño
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: El CTA tiene en cartera a un árbitro madrileño (de nacimiento y de colegio), Ortiz Arias, para el derbi madrileño del domingo. “Este al menos no tendrá video previo en RMTV”, me comentó un guasón. La decisión se enmarca en una estrategia de ‘desregionalización’ que pretende permitir que los equipos puedan tener árbitros de su propia regional. Hace decenios que se decidó evitar eso, en previsión de suspicacias, y a nadie le había preocupado. Pero a falta de arreglar las cosas que sí preocupan, y con la buena intención de colocar al fútbol en un plano más civilizado, han dado en esto. Ya se han hecho experimentos, aunque como el que mete el pie en el agua a ver cómo está de fría. Munuera Montero, andaluz, arbitró el derbi sevillano de noviembre de 2025; pero como es vecino de Jaén, a los efectos era como su viniera de Bilbao. Más arriesgado fue lo de García Verdura en el derbi barcelonés en enero de este año. Él si vive en Barcelona. Pero salió bien y no tuvo problemas. El domingo, si se confirma, tendremos a Ortiz Medina, que el lunes y el resto de la semana tendrá que salir en la calle a cruzarse con sus convecinos, que ya veremos cómo de contentos habrán quedado de su tarea. Y a saber si no empezarán a salir testimonios de si fue socio de tal o forofo de cual en el colegio. Puede ocurrir o no, pero esta estrategia me parece un postureo y un riesgo innecesario. Aparte de la que ‘desregionalización’ será creíble cuando un catalán arbitre un Clásico en el Bernabéu o un madrileño en el Camp Nou, y eso que ellos, llegado el caso, no tendrían que desayunar el lunes en la ciudad. Un ejemplo: esta semana tuvo un grave y oficialmente reconocido error el árbitro de VAR del derbi de Manchester, Matt Donohue, induciendo al árbitro a validar un gol ilegal a favor del City. Resulta que como profesor de Gresswell gestionó durante años la aportación de material deportivo del City al centro, lo que muchos han tomado como móvil y prueba de su parcialidad. ¿Hay necesidad de esto?

articles.title: Mou, segundas partes no son buenas
articles.standfirst: El Madrid no ha ganado ninguno de los últimos cuatro partidos contando sólo el segundo tiempo: tres derrotas, un empate, cinco goles en contra y sólo dos a favor
articles.summary: El Madrid no ha ganado ninguno de los últimos cuatro partidos contando sólo el segundo tiempo: tres derrotas, un empate, cinco goles en contra y sólo dos a favor
articles.body: Una luz amarilla se ha encendido en el panel de mando del Real Madrid. Un aviso de que algo no funciona bien que ha puesto en alerta a Mourinho. El problema ya ha causado un daño importante (la derrota ante el Betis) y amenaza con dejar al equipo fuera de combate si no se soluciona la 'avería'. El inconveniente está detectado, pero no solucionado. El Madrid se autodestruye en los segundos tiempos y lo que es una luz amarilla ya pudo ser roja ante el Elche. Llueve sobre mojado y los datos generan bastante inquietud, más allá de que las consecuencias no hayan sido muy graves. El Madrid ofrece una doble cara en su rendimiento y el partido ante el Elche llevó el problema a su máxima expresión: por la reiteración y por el susto que a punto estuvo de costarle dos puntos. Precisamente esta doble cara es la que ha amortiguado el problema, porque la buena puesta en escena del Madrid en los partidos le ha permitido 'sobrevivir' en casi todos ellos al caos más absoluto que se apodera del equipo tras el descanso. Los datos hablan por sí solos. De los siete partidos disputados, seis en Liga y uno en Champions, en los cuatro últimos el Madrid no gana contando sólo el segundo tiempo: sale perdiendo ante Elche (2-1), Inter (0-1), Betis (1-0) y empata frente al Rayo (1-1). De estos cuatro partidos, en tres de ellos la renta obtenida en el primer tiempo permitió al equipo de Mourinho sacar el partido adelante, no sin sufrimiento en los casos de Inter y Elche. Ante el Betis no tuvo el colchón de goles del primer tiempo y acabaría perdiendo. El otro balance en estos cuatro partidos, cinco goles en contra y sólo dos a favor en las segundas partes. Ante Málaga, Real y Espanyol el Madrid sí ganó el 'partido' del segundo tiempo, goleando en el del duelo ante los realistas. El caso es que el Madrid está jugando con fuego en las últimas semanas, que es cuando el problema se ha acentuado. El Madrid pasa de encarrilar los partidos a complicárselos, de jugar con una autoridad aplastante a dejarse comer la tostada, de disfrutar de marcadores favorables a ver cómo las ventajas desaparecen... En definitiva, a ganar con superioridad los primeros tiempos para luego perder en los segundos de una manera inexplicable. El Madrid pierde el control y con ello está poniendo en riesgo sus objetivos a largo plazo. Otra traspié ante el Elche hubiese supuesto un mazazo en la lucha por el título de Liga y con el Metropolitano como próxima parada. Mourinho parece tener claro el problema a falta de encontrar la solución. "El problema me parece obvio... Hay partidos que parecen acabados que no están acabados. La única explicación que encuentro es que son partidos fáciles, no matas... Partidos que no matamos y parece que pasamos de la facilidad a no controlar. Este tipo de estadio, lleno, afición fantástica... Lo ponen difícil. La cosa buena es que con la dificultad, el equipo reacciona y gana, que es lo más importante. Y cosa buena es que con los partidos del Madrid nadie se aburre, porque son muy divertidos", acabó bromeando. Pero de momento, segundas partes no son buenas en el Madrid.

articles.title: Marruecos justifica a Abde tras su apoyo a Ceuta: "Fue un desliz, pura torpeza"
articles.standfirst: Mohamed Ouahbi, seleccionador de Marruecos, zanja la polémica sobre Abde y su decisión de lucir una camiseta con el lema "Todos somos caballas" para apoyar a Ceuta
articles.summary: Mohamed Ouahbi, seleccionador de Marruecos, zanja la polémica sobre Abde y su decisión de lucir una camiseta con el lema "Todos somos caballas" para apoyar a Ceuta
articles.body: Mohamed Ouahbi, seleccionador de Marruecos, habló en rueda de prensa sobre la decisión del futbolista marroquí Ez Abde de lucir en el estadio de La Cerámica la camiseta con el lema "Todos somos caballas" para apoyar a la población de Ceuta. El delantero del Real Betis, que en 2021 parecía que elegía jugar con España y que meses después escogió defender los colores de Marruecos, fue víctima de insultos y amenazas ("Traidor, cobarde, Ceuta es Marruecos...") en sus redes sociales por ponerse la camiseta. Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, más conocido como Ez Abde, nacido en Beni Mellal (Marruecos) y criado en Elche (Alicante), explicó posteriormente en un comunicado que "primero quiero dejar clara una cosa, en ningún momento se ha utilizado la camiseta referente al pueblo de Ceuta con un objetivo político o de desprecio hacia mi pueblo, el pueblo marroquí. Esta era una camiseta de carácter social en apoyo a una población y sus habitantes, independientemente de su nacionalidad, que estaban viviendo una situación complicada. Ahora bien, esto no es una disculpa ante nadie y todo aquel que desee usar esto para dudar de mi amor por mi país es libre de hacerlo, yo seguiré viviendo cada día con la cabeza bien alta y seguiré representando con orgullo y sacrificio mis raíces". Abde, con la polémica ya olvidada, marcó el gol del triunfo del Real Betis por 1-0 contra el Getafe. Mohamed Ouahbi definió como "un desliz" y "pura torpeza" la decisión de Abde, que ha sido 37 veces internacional con Marruecos, de ponerse la camiseta con el lema "Todos somos caballas" para apoyar a la población de Ceuta. "Abde, simplemente fue un desliz. Ya se pronunció y difundió una breve declaración. Fue pura torpeza. Nadie puede arrebatarle su amor por Marruecos ni su compromiso con la selección nacional y con Marruecos", afirmó el seleccionador de 'Los Leones del Atlas'. Mohamed Ouahbi destacó que aunque "la política influye en el fútbol", no desea implicarse en ella: "Intentamos mantenernos al margen". "Necesitamos encontrar las mejores soluciones para brindar orientación y prevención. Me pongo en su lugar (el de Abde): estaba ansioso por jugar su primer partido con Marruecos desde el Mundial, y le dan una camiseta en el vestuario… Para mí, el asunto está zanjado", sentenció Ouahbi, que ha convocado a Abde para jugar con Marruecos los dos partidos eliminatorios ante Gabón y Lesoto de clasificación para la Copa Africana de Naciones.

articles.title: Alexander Isak: Moving from Newcastle to Liverpool was an 'easy decision'
articles.summary: Striker Alexander Isak says Liverpool's ambition and determination to sign him was a big part of why he joined the club.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak says joining Liverpool last summer was an "easy decision".

The Sweden striker arrived from Newcastle on transfer deadline day in September 2025 for a British record transfer fee of £125m.

"[ Liverpool ] is a massive club, and everything about the club made it pretty clear," he told BBC Sport's The Football Interview.

"And the club's ambition and the club's will to get me in as well. It was a big part of it."

Isak missed pre-season last summer and trained at his former club Real Sociedad amid uncertainty around his Newcastle future, saying promises made to him there had been "broken".

However, he struggled for goals in his first season at Anfield before a leg break ruled him out from December to April.

This season the 26-year-old has already matched last season's tally of three Premier League goals, after only four games.

Asked if there was ever a point last season when he regretted the move, Isak replied: "No, never. I would never think like that."

He added: "[The leg break] was tough. Anyone who had a long injury would know. But on the other hand, when you're in a good place and when you feel good, you don't really tend to look back because it doesn't really benefit you.

"So I'm just looking forward and feel really optimistic and excited about the season, and what it can bring to us."

Over the summer, Isak made his World Cup bow for Sweden after managing just 1,032 minutes for Liverpool over 22 appearances last season.

He scored once and assisted three goals for Graham Potter's side before they were knocked out by France in the last 32.

"Playing for your country in a World Cup is a dream of most people," said Isak.

"With the injuries last season, the World Cup was perfect. I had that period where I could play and gain rhythm and form.

"And, on top of that, it was a massive experience, so that was perfect to do and come back here for pre-season and to start the season."

Defending from front is Liverpool's 'attacking weapon'

New Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer, has told Isak that he wants him to defend from the front as it is an "attacking weapon" for Liverpool .

"He asks me to be part of the defending but to defend in positions where, when we win the ball, we can counter quickly and get the ball forward to the offensive line," said Isak.

"He said 'score goals', but he wants me to defend. The way we defend - we defend to score goals so defending, in the end, is an attacking weapon."

Under Iraola, Liverpool are aiming to implement a front-foot and aggressive style of football. They have made the most sprints in the Premier League this season.

"He came with his football - the way he wants to play and the high intensity which I think will benefit me, the club and the way the club wants to play football," added Isak.

On the style of football since Iraola joined, Isak says: "I think that's what the team needs. It's not just about getting the ball to me, it's about getting the ball forward and to all of the offensive players quickly.

"I think that will benefit the team. I think if we can do that then we should score more goals."

And Isak, who has 60 Premier League goals to his name, is determined to help bring silverware to Liverpool this year but insisted he is not someone who sets personal targets.

His most prolific Premier League season came with Newcastle in 2024-25 when he scored 23 goals.

"Everyone knows that success for this club is winning trophies," said Isak. "I want to score every game. Everyone is different. Some like to set targets and some don't. I'm the one that doesn't."

articles.title: Why Spurs are struggling to score goals and what next?
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are yet to score a Premier League goal this season, how do they fix that?
articles.body:
Four games into the season, Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City are the only sides yet to score in the Premier League.

Spurs have brought in £320m worth of talent – a bulk of that in attacking reinforcements – so why are they struggling to score?

We analysed the tactics Roberto de Zerbi is trying to implement and what potential fixes may look like.

While the Premier League looks different to when De Zerbi left Brighton in 2024, the Italian has shown clear signs of adapting while retaining his tactical principles.

De Zerbi's sides entice opponents to apply pressure – often through slowing down play and passing the ball backwards.

They then react to the opponents' movements by speeding up play, looking to take advantage of the spaces behind the pressing players through direct passing or powerful carrying.

In a 2020 coaching seminar, De Zerbi explained: "The stronger the pressure of the opponent, the more vertical [our] action becomes. [The fewer opponents behind], the easier it becomes to go and score."

We have seen De Zerbi's forwards in bigger spaces facing fewer defenders on numerous occasions this season already.

Turning build-up play to goals, however, requires many parts to come together.

Spurs' shape in possession can be hard to read but it often looks like a 2-3-2-3.

The holding midfielder, usually Rodrigo Bentancur, anchors the midfield in front of Spurs' two central defenders with this trio remaining fairly fixed.

The 2-3-2-3 shape generally stays the same but there is rotation between the wingers, full-backs and central midfielders.

In rotating, players are encouraged to maintain the side's shape by swapping zones with their team-mates – filling gaps as they arise.

On top of these positional rules, De Zerbi gives his sides principles to implement.

A lot of what he is doing worked well during his time at Marseille - from 2024 to 2026 - where they averaged 2.3 goals per game.

It might not be happening for De Zerbi yet this season at Tottenham . But they might not be that far off.

Glimpses of Spurs' central play but work required

De Zerbi encourages his players to play centrally.

When Spurs' centre-backs are on the ball, opposing midfielders and forwards begin to push up, creating space for Spurs' attacking midfielders between the lines.

The other effect this central play has is that it can draw the defending team in-field, which opens up space in the wide areas for Spurs' direct wingers to attack.

When playing these passes into the middle, a few things have to align.

Players receiving the pass have to be comfortable doing so under pressure and naturally, some are more suited to these constraints.

Recognising that Sandro Tonali is better in big space facing forwards, we have seen him rotate positions with Archie Gray, who starts at right-back - a sensible tweak.

Although not his natural position, the 20-year-old has managed in these tight spaces and appears to understand the tactical demands of his manager.

The return of James Maddison, who came back from a shoulder injury for last Tuesday's Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool , will provide De Zerbi with a player better suited to these spaces and in turn help get Spurs into attacking zones more often.

Individual player quality aside, much of the success of this approach will come down to players internalising their manager's instructions.

And it will take time for some of the squad to unlearn the habits they developed under previous coaches.

At the start of last season under Thomas Frank, Spurs built up primarily down the flanks, almost skipping the centre of the pitch entirely. The logic then was to avoid the risk associated with turnovers in the middle of the pitch.

De Zerbi is actively coaching an unorthodox style that goes against these instructions - but getting players to be brave enough to play in congested areas may take some time.

Spurs' build-up has regularly got them in positions behind the opposition midfield by attacking quickly after they are pressed.

Turning these great attacking situations into goals has been one of Spurs' biggest issues.

There are three parts to this. The first is the ability to recognise the best pass available. This depends the second element - the movement of players ahead of them. Thirdly, players need to have the ability to execute the pass.

Spurs' biggest bottleneck so far has been in players either failing to recognise or opting not to play through balls in behind.

The attacking runs, particularly from Omar Marmoush, have generally been good but passes haven't always followed.

Gray has attempted to feed passes down the line but Spurs have not done this regularly more centrally.

Pedro Porro, known for his ability to create chances, took up a more central role in possession for Spain this summer as they won the World Cup.

As he returns, his natural tendencies, which suit these tactics, may help Spurs create more goalscoring chances.

They might then get some of the joy that De Zerbi's forwards had at Marseille.

But while Porro gets up to speed, others in the Tottenham team are still getting to grips with the runs expected of them.

During De Zerbi's time at Marseille, diagonal runs from wide attackers on the last line, found by willing vertical passers, worked as a way of finding goals.

Igor Paixao's goal in Marseille's 2-2 draw with Toulouse last season is a strong example of these ideas working well, with De Zerbi's former club displaying a good understanding of direct passing and well-timed off-ball movement.

Similarly, against Liverpool on Tuesday, we saw Destiny Udogie get into good positions on the left flank.

Although Andy Robertson has played well for Tottenham this season, Udogie's physicality and timing helped him exploit space when the game became stretched.

This allowed Spurs to get into crossing positions against a disorganised Liverpool shape.

When an attacking side accelerate play, it is common for the defending team to drop back in an urgent manner, looking to protect their goal.

When this happens, space opens up in front of the defence, for late-arriving midfielders or clever strikers that drop back.

Again, Marmoush has tried to do this on a number of occasions but has not always been found.

This may be a matter of players requiring time to gel. For Savio, it may also be a wide player struggling to pull the ball back on their weak foot.

Left-footed right-winger Savio is better at getting to the byeline but the left-footed Udogie and Robertson have created clearer chances via crosses.

At Marseille, both right winger and right full-back were comfortable cutting the ball back on their right foot.

These crosses were maximised by the excellent box-movement of 37-year-old Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

Looking at how De Zerbi is trying to work, it is easier to see how many of Tottenham 's attacking moves are almost there in terms of creating clearer chances.

This is not to say things will be perfect immediately. Successful tactics depend on a team's quality - and Marseille's forwards were excellent finishers who thrived in space.

But if the small details across the pitch are refined, Spurs should create enough chances to score, even if they miss a few.

articles.title: Luke Littler: What world No 1 needs to complete darts majors clean sweep in 2026 to make more history
articles.summary: Luke Littler needs to win five more titles to complete a clean sweep of major darts titles in 2026; watch the World Grand Prix from September 28 to October 4, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Littler has the World Championship, World Masters, UK Open and World Matchplay titles under his belt already to add to an already crowded 2026 trophy cabinet that also includes the Premier League and World Cup.

He now has to win five more titles to make more history, so Sky Sports analyses Littler's exact path to achieving that historic feat...

Littler's next hurdle on the journey to the clean sweep begins on Friday at the World Series of Darts finals.

Michael van Gerwen is the reigning champion, having beaten Littler 11-7 in front of a partisan home crowd in Amsterdam, but the Englishman does have a World Series title under his belt already, having beaten Michael Smith 11-4 in 2024.

Over a week later, Littler will have the World Grand Prix to contend with, live on Sky Sports from September 28 to October 4, where he faces a challenging tie against Luke Woodhouse in the first round.

Littler has previously established that he "didn't like" the double-in, double-out format of the tournament , bemoaning the Grand Prix as "one of the toughest tournaments to win, with the Worlds, the Matchplay, [and] the Premier League".

That format change, though, did not stop Littler from winning 6-1 in the 2025 final in a dominant performance against world No 2 Luke Humphries.

His journey will then take him to Dortmund, where he will seek to win the one major title that has eluded him in his career thus far - the European Championship, where he suffered a 10-7 second-round defeat at the hands of James Wade in the last edition in 2025.

Should Littler win that title, he would hold all of darts' major titles - something no one else has done (as Van Gerwen nearly did it in 2016 and 2017 but did not win the World Cup of Darts).

Littler then would have to win a third straight Grand Slam title in Wolverhampton, before taking a trip to Minehead to retain the Players Championship, where he beat Nathan Aspinall 11-8 in the 2025 final.

If the teenager wins all of those titles, he would become the first player to win every darts major in the same calendar year.

How can Littler qualify for the Players Championship Finals?

Littler has significant work to do on the Pro Tour to stand any chance of securing the Players Championship - and, by extension, the clean sweep.

He is ranked 125th on the Players Championship Order of Merit with just £10,500 in prize winnings thus far - only the top 64 qualify for the finals weekend at Minehead.

Shane McGuirk sits in 64th with £27,500 in winnings with just six Players Championship events in the calendar left, meaning the reigning champion would have to make up at least £17,500 in winnings in order to qualify.

This is still a feasible target for Littler, with the winner of each event adding £15,000 to their kitty - so he probably has to win just one of the six remaining events - and accumulate some prize money in the others - to stand a chance of retaining his title.

The world No 1 was hoping to do much of the work in August, when he returned to the floor events in Leicester after missing the first 26 Players Championships, but he only managed to reach a quarter-final and a semi-final in his two appearances.

Littler will fancy his chances to make up the deficit in prize money with six events in Den Bosch and Leicester remaining - but the clock is starting to tick.

articles.title: Spiders still climbing - watch Queen's Park v Ayr United on BBC Scotland & iPlayer
articles.summary: Sportscene's Jonathan Sutherland previews Friday's live BBC Scotland TV match as Queen's Park host Ayr United.
articles.body:
As Mark Twain almost certainly never said, news of Queen's Park's demise has been greatly exaggerated.

When reports emerged last year that Lord William Haughey was ending his financial agreement with Scotland's oldest football club, the general assumption was the Spiders might easily slip away back down the Scottish Professional Football League web back to lower league obscurity.

Not so. Instead, Sean Crighton's side remained defiant last season as they came close to flirting with the promotion play-off places before finishing a commendable sixth.

Yes, the Queen's Park academy may be no more, but the under-17s and under-19s sides are thriving - both won their respective leagues last season.

And businessman Haughey's presence remains in the background, with his City Charitable Trust helping transform the club's impressive Lochinch training ground in the heart of Glasgow's Pollok Park.

"One thing we've got here is a great training centre," manager Crighton says.

"And, obviously, at Lesser Hampden, the pitch is unbelievable. We've got the facilities - we need to be a good Championship team."

They are also a Championship team that is very much buying into the brave new Craig Mulholland Scottish FA vision of developing young Scottish talent, with a view to the balance sheet.

Queen's Park helped both Scotland captain Andy Robertson and Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland earn themselves some valuable early steps in senior football. Helping emerging talent flourish is something Crighton is keen to continue and develop.

"Josh Fowler's moved on to St Johnstone, doing well in the Premiership," Crighton points out. "Seb Drozd has moved on to Partick Thistle - he's flying over there. Henry Fieldson's gone to St Mirren.

"We've got a barrowload of them [this season]. Young Ross McLean has come into the team last year a couple of times and progressed well this year. He's a manager's dream, he's very versatile – he can play in the middle, he can play wide, he can play at the back.

"Tyrece McDonnell as well. I think he made 26 appearances last season."

And the manager added: "We need to be that club because that's Queen's Park's history. The guys that are in the national team, they started at Queen's Park.

"When I got the job, that was it from the outset. It was, 'Can you help players progress?' Not just me, everyone in the building. That's what we want to try and do.

"I've got a sense of pride that we've managed to have these players play for us and then move on."

Who has your Championship club brought in & let go? - Summer 2026

On the pitch, central midfielder Scott Martin - a relative veteran now at the age of 29 - is also impressed by the level of emerging Scottish talent he sees around him.

"Young Aiden McCallion [co-operation loan from Rangers], he's a central midfielder as well," Martin says. "He's been great since he came through the door, gets on with his work, very tidy on the ball. Same with Lewis Stewart [also co-operation loan from Rangers], he's lightning.

"At Rangers, they must be so used to dominating the ball and having time. But here in the Championship it's a totally different game. It's end-to-end, it's high intensity.

"It will be a great experience for them because they're learning a totally different side of the game that maybe you wouldn't learn at a B team or an under-19s or 20s, whatever it might be. The way they have fitted in has been absolutely top notch."

After a good League Cup group campaign, the start of the Championship season has been more challenging for Queen's Park. They currently find themselves second bottom of the table.

However, Martin is in no doubt they have what it takes to stay in the division again this season as they prepare to host an Ayr United side one place and one point above them.

"Anybody can beat anybody," Martin added before Friday's BBC Scotland TV match.

"We've had a lot of difficult games, but I think the Partick Thistle game was our turning point [0-0 draw] in the sense that we found that belief that we can go to, in my opinion, the hardest place in the Championship and grab a point.

"In terms of where we are this season, I think we're OK. There's been parts of games where we play really, really well. It's just trying to put that all together and be more consistent.

"We've got a youngish squad at times as well, so it can be a bit difficult, but we're not far away from being a right good side again."

articles.title: FPL gameweek five tips: Keep or sell Man City's Rayan Cherki?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers in gameweek five.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek five.

Is it time to acquire Nottingham Forest assets?

Yes, absolutely. They face Coventry in gameweek five and their fixtures after that are decent too (apart from the Arsenal fixture on 18 October).

Morgan Gibbs-White (£8.0m) is their talisman. He plays 90 minutes regularly, takes their penalties and is heavily involved in their attacking play. New signing Daniel Munoz (£5.4m) was very unlucky not to register at least one assist last game and Neco Williams (£5.0m) also has very good attacking threat.

Liam Delap (£5.5m) is an interesting one. He looked good against Aston Villa last weekend but I still worry about his minutes with the likes of Igor Jesus (£5.8m) and Chris Wood (£5.8m) potentially eating into his game time.

Newcastle have a promising set of fixtures - should I invest?

My top three Newcastle picks are Lewis Hall (£5.2m), Yoane Wissa (£6.2m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.0m).

Szoboszlai will come good in FPL. He's on penalties, corners and has quality shooting from outside the box. He can even chip in with defensive contributions too, so he's an easy hold for me.

articles.summary: Arsenal January Transfer Window: Forward Search Back in Focus for Mikel ArtetaArsenal are already being pointed towards a familiar issue, the need to act dec...
articles.body:
Arsenal January Transfer Window: Forward Search Back in Focus for Mikel Arteta

Arsenal are already being pointed towards a familiar issue, the need to act decisively in the January transfer window. According to Football London , there is a growing sense that Mikel Arteta and the club cannot afford another winter market without meaningful first-team reinforcement, especially in attack.

The central point is hard to ignore. "In 2026, 2025 and 2024, the Gunners didn't make a single signing to their senior squads in the winter market." Context matters, of course. Arsenal have previously found themselves limited by finances, availability and timing, all of which can shape a January strategy before it properly begins.

That challenge has already been evident in their recent recruitment work. The report notes that Antoine Semenyo was among the players Arsenal admired, but " Man City were the only viable option to make a move earlier this year, while Arsenal and Liverpool would've had to wait until the summer." It is a useful reminder that admiration and execution are very different things in the market.

Arsenal also tried to strengthen further forward in the most recent summer window. "Arsenal wanted to add another forward and made moves for Morgan Rogers , Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez , all of which, however, proved fruitless for a variety of reasons." That line carries weight, particularly when set against the departures of Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli , with Christos Tzolis the only incoming addition in that area.

Attention has now shifted to the current alternatives. " Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres , therefore, have maintained their places in the squad as the second-choice left winger and centre-forward." Yet their outings against Ipswich Town brought scrutiny, with "Gyokeres in particular" under the spotlight. That naturally sharpens discussion around depth, reliability and whether Arsenal have enough proven support if injuries hit the regular starters.

The complication, as ever, is that January is rarely straightforward. "The market is notoriously difficult to do ideal business in," and suitable forwards are often scarce, expensive and expected to deliver immediately. Football London adds that " Eli Junior Kroupi and Kevin Schade are both names to monitor," which may prove significant if Arsenal revisit the market with urgency.

From an Arsenal supporter's perspective, this feels like a warning that should be heeded early rather than explained away later. We have seen too many windows where the need was obvious, the options were known, and the club still came out of January without the extra quality required to sustain a title push or survive setbacks.

If the club genuinely believed another forward was needed in the summer, and the report makes clear they did, then the logic has not suddenly disappeared. In fact, it may have become even stronger. Letting two experienced wide options go and replacing them with only one addition always carried risk. When backup attackers then struggle to convince, the conversation becomes unavoidable.

There is still time for Arsenal to shape this properly. The key is preparation. Supporters will accept that January is difficult, but they will not accept being unprepared for it. If top targets are unavailable, the recruitment team must already have realistic alternatives lined up, whether that means a Premier League-proven option, a younger profile with upside, or a short-term solution who can contribute straight away.

Above all, Arsenal cannot allow ambition to drift because the market is awkward. Clubs competing at the top solve problems before they become defining weaknesses. If there is a dream forward chase to reignite, then the groundwork must start now.
