articles.title: Matias - The Comeback
articles.summary: Seven years in purgatory. The two-legged tie against Schalke 04 in the 2011 Champions League quarter-finals was memorable. The match was remembered for Stank...
articles.body:
Seven years in purgatory. The two-legged tie against Schalke 04 in the 2011 Champions League quarter-finals was memorable. The match was remembered for Stankovic's goal from the halfway line, but also for the countless counter-attacking opportunities handed to the Germans. It marked the final chapter for an extraordinary team that had lifted the trophy into the Madrid sky.

From there, a return to Europe's elite seemed a formality, then an important objective, and eventually almost a pipe dream.

The seven-year drought, an almost biblical number, came to an end on a May night at the Olimpico, when a quirk of the fixture list had turned the final matchday, Lazio vs. Inter , into something resembling a Champions League play-off. Inter had only one possible outcome: victory. And it came courtesy of a header from the least expected man: Matías Vecino , a midfielder by trade who had a penchant for scoring important goals. Riccardo Trevisani summed it up perfectly in commentary: Vecino gets it. 3-2, and Inter are back in the Champions League.

The return to the Champions League in September was billed as a gala occasion. The Club's season-ticket campaign quoted Dante: back to see the stars. San Siro was buzzing; it felt like one of those nights when something magical was about to happen. As the competition's anthem finished at the start of the match, a roar went up that seemed to shake the very foundations of the stadium.

But then Tottenham took the lead, courtesy of a cruel deflection from Christian Eriksen 's shot — a player we would see around these parts again. Alongside the Dane, Tottenham had stars such as Harry Kane , Son and Lucas Moura . That edition would see them go all the way to the final. But San Siro refused to surrender. The equaliser arrived almost by chance. Five minutes from time, Mauro Icardi took a knock and stopped just outside the edge of the penalty arc, despite practically living inside the box. The ball dropped in front of him; he did not hesitate and struck it sweetly on the volley. 1-1.

It was not over. In stoppage time, Inter won a corner. Miranda rose to meet it with his head. The ball seemed magnetically drawn towards a player waiting in the six-yard box, who calmly turned it into the net. It was a roar that would live long in the memory. Once again, Trevisani had a moment of inspiration as he called the goal. Just a few words that, even today, immediately transport anyone who hears them back to that exact moment: Vecino's got it again.

The statement was clear: Inter were not the strongest team in the Champions League, they would fail to reach the last 16 in that edition but from then on, every opponent would have to reckon with them. And since 2018, when it all began, that has indeed remained the case.

articles.title: Raúl Varela señala el gran problema de España: "Lo de Zubimendi es algo difícil de explicar"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu analiza los posibles retoques de Luis de la Fuente en el inicio del nuevo ciclo de la campeona del mundo
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu analiza los posibles retoques de Luis de la Fuente en el inicio del nuevo ciclo de la campeona del mundo
articles.body: España vuelve a escena como campeona del mundo y Raúl Varela analizó en La Tribu el escenario que se abre para Luis de la Fuente antes de que el seleccionador vuelva a tomar la palabra. Una nueva etapa en la que, según el periodista, no deberían producirse demasiados cambios de inicio, aunque ya aparecen algunas situaciones que obligan a estar atentos. "Aparentemente no habrá grandes novedades. No hay motivo para ello. Primero porque los campeones merecen honores y estrenar el nuevo ciclo y segundo porque siguen siendo en la mayor parte de los casos los mejores en sus respectivos puestos y para el equipo", explicó Varela. El periodista recordó que España afrontará este nuevo periodo con Inglaterra, Croacia y República Checa como rivales y con partidos en Londres, Split, Praga, Oviedo, Sevilla y el Metropolitano de Madrid. Uno de los puntos en los que puso especialmente el foco fue el centro del campo. "Quizá el mayor problema en el largo plazo aparezca en nuestra sala de máquinas. A Rodri hay que cuidarlo y mimarlo y lo de Zubimendi es algo difícil de explicar", señaló. Varela recordó el papel del centrocampista en los dos grandes títulos recientes de la selección: "Casi inédito en los dos grandes éxitos de De la Fuente, Euro en Alemania y el pasado Campeonato del Mundo, acabó aportando minutos de calidad en las dos finales donde tuvo que jugar por extrema necesidad y sin apenas tiempo para entrar en calor". Su situación actual en el Arsenal es la que provoca las dudas del periodista. "Ahora en el Arsenal vive un momento realmente oscuro. Arteta lo usó en el último compromiso copero como lateral. Algo se ha roto en Londres que no sabemos si podrá recomponerse. Hay que estar alerta". También aparecen posibles movimientos en otras posiciones. En la portería, Varela señaló que, pendientes de la rodilla de Joan García, existen alternativas: "Leo Román, el propio Remiro o esa novedad que supone Josep Martínez bajo los palos del Inter conceden margen". Todo ello en una posición que "sigue siendo de Unai, candidato a mejor portero del año y de Raya que sigue siendo de lo mejor que te puedes echar a la cara". La retirada de Llorente también abre un hueco que deberá cubrir De la Fuente. Varela plantea la posibilidad de apostar por alguno de los jóvenes laterales o recuperar centrales que se quedaron fuera, con Pubill o Eric García como opciones para desplazarse a la banda. Y vuelve también el debate habitual alrededor del delantero centro. "Luego, la eterna duda de la delantera donde todo nos parece un problema hasta que llega 'Oyarhaaland' y mete media docena de goles sin ni siquiera molestarse en celebrarlos con una leve sonrisa", afirmó. Varela destacó además que "Ferran aterrizó de pie en París" y valoró la aparición de otros nombres: "Que Roberto Fernández, Sergio Camello o Carlos Espí estén acaparando titulares siempre es bueno para fomentar la competencia". Además, dejó abierta la puerta a nuevas incorporaciones: "Hay que hacerle hueco a Fermín y quien sabe si a alguno más". El periodista cerró su intervención poniendo el foco en el regreso de la selección después de conquistar el Mundial: "Hoy vuelve España. Hoy vuelve la campeona del mundo".

articles.title: Stats: Raphinha has turned penalties into a near-guaranteed goal for Barcelona
articles.summary: Raphinha has developed into one of Barcelona’s most reliable players from the penalty spot, and his record explains why he continues to be trusted when the p...
articles.body:
Raphinha has developed into one of Barcelona 's most reliable players from the penalty spot, and his record explains why he continues to be trusted when the pressure is highest.

As per Mundo Deportivo , the Brazilian has taken 22 penalties during his career and missed only once. That solitary failure came back in 2017, when he was playing for Vitoria Guimaraes.

His record since arriving at Barcelona is even cleaner: 13 penalties, 13 goals.

The two he converted against Racing Santander were particularly interesting because they broke a pattern he had followed for most of his time in Spain.

Raphinha rarely gives goalkeepers the same answer

Raphinha, currently negotiating his Barcelona renewal , has generally avoided going to the same side twice with Barcelona. His first penalty for the club came against Real Sociedad in the 2023/24 season, when he sent the ball low to the goalkeeper's right.

From there, he began alternating, although there was one obvious interruption: the Panenka against Sevilla.

Otherwise, the pattern was remarkably consistent. Raphinha would stay relatively close to the ball, keep his run-up compact and strike low and firmly towards the corner.

Against Racing, however, after converting his first penalty by going right, he went the same way again with his second.

Interestingly, Racing goalkeeper Julien Agirrezabala guessed incorrectly on both occasions, leaving Raphinha's spotless Barcelona penalty record intact.

Only Lewandowski has taken more for Barça

Raphinha is not Barcelona's most frequent penalty taker since his arrival, as that honour belongs to Robert Lewandowski, who has taken 19 and scored 16.

Raphinha is next with 13 from 13, followed by Lamine Yamal with seven from nine. Dani Olmo has also converted both of his attempts.

Ferran Torres has missed once, while Pedri , Ansu Fati , Franck Kessie and Ilkay Gundogan have each scored from the spot, with the latter also missing another.

The numbers certainly explain Raphinha's importance, but his consistency is what separates him. Goalkeepers can study his previous attempts, look for patterns and try to anticipate the decision.

However, Raphinha has made that job harder.

articles.title: Bayern Munich superstar expects Real Madrid ‘to get better’ under Jose Mourinho: ‘I have a lot of respect for him’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho’s return to Real Madrid as manager at the beginning of the summer has added a buzz around what the club can achieve this season.The Portuguese...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho's return to Real Madrid as manager at the beginning of the summer has added a buzz around what the club can achieve this season.

The Portuguese tactician has always been a maverick wherever he has been during his long career, and even other clubs want to see what Mourinho can do in his second spell.

Bayern Munich superstar Harry Kane has weighed in on the same. The Englishman believes Jose Mourinho has made Real Madrid an even more difficult opponent in the Champions League.

Kane also spoke warmly about Jude Bellingham and discussed his own place in a Ballon d'Or race that includes Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe .

Kane has a beautiful relationship with Jose

Speaking to MARCA , Kane reflected on his experience under Mourinho before assessing what the Portuguese coach could now bring to Madrid.

The England national team captain played some of his finest football under Mourinho at Tottenham and clearly retains enormous respect for him.

Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane shared an excellent relationship at the 2026 World Cup. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

"Yes, I love Jose. We had a really good relationship at Tottenham. It didn't end the way we wanted and the fact that Jose didn't get the opportunity to manage that final was tough. It was difficult for me too," he said.

"But yes, I had a very good relationship with him. I played some of my best games at Tottenham during his time. I won the Golden Boot and also the award for most assists in the same year."

Kane then explained why he thrived so much under the Portuguese manager.

"He gave me a lot of freedom to be myself, to play and to drop deep. And I think, as a person, he is someone who understands every detail of the game, whether it's with the ball, without the ball, tactically, with the referee… whatever it is, he understands every situation," Kane explained.

"I have a lot of respect for him. It's true that we haven't seen each other much since he left Tottenham, but maybe this year we'll face each other in the Champions League and it will be good to meet again."

Kane expects Madrid to get better under Jose

Kane was then asked directly whether Mourinho's presence makes Real Madrid a more difficult opponent for Bayern.

"Real have signed good players and Mou is a great coach who will get the best out of the players he has," he explained.

Harry Kane had an excellent time at Tottenham Hotspur under Jose Mourinho. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

"Real Madrid always have some of the best players in the world, and this year is no different, just like the previous one. We know there is a good chance we'll face them later in the competition."

Kane then spoke about the prospect of facing Madrid in the latter stages of the Champions League.

"Real Madrid, in the Champions League, are always going to be there in the latter rounds. We came out on top against them last year, but we also know it was a very difficult tie. And with Jose now it will be even more difficult," Kane said.

Kane knows exactly how Jose can galvanise a dressing room and why that mentality matters on the biggest occasions.

Kane knew Bellingham and Mourinho would connect

Kane also discussed Jude Bellingham's excellent start and revealed that Mourinho had been a topic of conversation between the England team-mates during the World Cup.

"Jude and I had a really good connection at the World Cup, because of the way we played and passed the ball to each other. Great connection with and without the ball," Kane said.

"And off the pitch we also built a really strong relationship, and that can only help the national team."

The Englishman then offered insight into his conversation with Jude regarding Mourinho.

"It's great to see how well he has adapted to Madrid. I spoke to him a little during the World Cup about Jose Mourinho, and I knew he was going to love Mourinho," he said.

"And I knew Jose would love Jude, and obviously it looks like they already have a good relationship. Jude has started brilliantly. And from an England point of view, it's fantastic to see that."

That mutual admiration is hardly surprising. Bellingham's intensity, personality and willingness to influence every phase of a match make him the type of player Mourinho has always valued enormously.

Kane is among the leading names being discussed for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, alongside candidates including Madrid's Mbappe.

Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe are set to go head-to-head for the Ballon d'Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Asked about his case after scoring 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England during 2025-26, Kane refused to campaign aggressively for himself.

"It's complicated. I've never liked talking too much about myself. The only thing I would say is that last season was incredible, personally and as a team. It was, by far, the best season of my life," he said.

"It's true that reaching 73 goals, the second-highest figure in history, speaks for itself. I'm extremely proud of it. I can only thank my teammates and everyone who helped me make it possible."

"But the Ballon d'Or isn't in my hands. It depends on the people who vote. From my point of view, last season is already in the past.

" Now I'm focused on this one and I'm looking forward to seeing what more I can do. I know there will be a lot of talk about the Ballon d'Or until October, because it's a great award."

It was then pointed out that the ceremony is going to be staged in London, which had been Kane's home for many years.

"Yes, a lot of people have told me that and maybe it's a good omen. Of course, having it in my hometown would make it even more special. So yes, it's a strange feeling that it's being held there this year. We'll have to wait and see what happens," he concluded.

Kane is arguably the favourite for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but both Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have positioned themselves aggressively .

If one were to combine individual numbers and silverware as criteria for the award, it is very difficult to look past the Englishman.

However, Mbappe's ridiculous season and Lamine's World Cup victory could also see some votes tilt towards them.

It remains to be seen who the award eventually goes to and whether Kane gets to face Jose Mourinho's side in the latter stages of the Champions League this year.

articles.title: Who will be the first EPL manager to be sacked this season? Carrick lands on unwanted podium
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is now considered among the three most likely Premier League managers to be sacked next.The Red Devils gathered more p...
articles.body:
Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is now considered among the three most likely Premier League managers to be sacked next.

The Red Devils gathered more points than any other club last season when the 45-year-old tactician took over from Ruben Amorim.

The returning club legend propelled Man Utd from 7th place to third in the table, ensuring Champions League qualification with a rather comfortable margin.

Carrick's exploits last term earned him the permanent role, but the situation has drastically differed this season.

While some had tipped Man Utd to enter the title discussion based on last season's form, these hopes were swiftly dashed, as the club has only gathered four points in as many Premier League fixtures.

In their last league outing, they lost to a Manchester City side that played with a man down for the bulk of the game.

United followed it up by crashing out of the Carabao Cup after squandering an early two-goal lead against Brighton , who pounced on their hosts' shambolic defending to complete a shocking turnaround.

According to Oddschecker , the odds of Man Utd sacking their head coach went from 9/1 to 10/3 following the defeat to Brighton.

Hence, the 45-year-old is now considered the third most likely Premier League manager to be sacked next.

Alvaro Arbeloa is the huge favourite (1/2), as his Fulham has only picked up a point in four weeks. Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is the second in line. Although the newly-promoted side has yet to register a point, the Chelsea icon still has some credit from last season's achievements.

Would it be fair to sack Michael Carrick?

After an underwhelming transfer market, Man Utd fans rallied around Carrick, realising his mission will be rather difficult, with the management failing to plug some of the holes in the squad, especially at left-back.

But regardless of the hierarchy's obvious blunders, much more has been expected from the head coach and his players this season.

Thanks to his status as a club legend and his solid performances last season, Carrick should be able to buy himself extra time, but unless he can turn things around in the coming weeks, we could be about to witness a third mid-season managerial change in as many years at Carrington.

articles.title: Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen skeptical of rotation
articles.summary: FC Bayern is not a club to take its foot off the gas.
articles.body:
Does Bayern Munich need to make like the champions and go the way of Paris Saint-Germain — frequently rotating players in a less-than-competitive domestic league in order to make a bid for Champions League glory?

Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen doesn't think so.

"Competition is really good for us and we need a challenge in the league," Dreesen explained for SPORT1-Doppelpass, as captured by @iMiaSanMia . "I remember well during Pep Guardiola's time with us, we played Augsburg in 2015. I don't remember which matchday it was, but we had qualified for the Champions League semifinals — and he played with a B team against Augsburg. We obviously lost — and also lost the semifinal.

"I don't think it works like that. I don't think you can calculate it that way. And I also don't think you can fine-tune workload management so precisely that the players are exactly at their peak and able to deliver their full 100% [in the Champions League]. That's why competition is good for us. It pushes us to perform even better."

Clearly, the concept of going easy does not fit into Bayern's mentality.

But…Bayern has been rotating. Kompany's prioritizing the Champions League already, and his substitutions have already resulted in dropped points. While Bayern took care of business, emphatically , against Norwegian giant-slayers Bodø/Glimt, Bayern drew 0-0 to Schalke and escaped with a 2-1 win over SV Elversberg — two newly-promoted Bundesliga sides. Harry Kane and Michael Olise started from the bench in the former, while Joshua Kimmich , Luis Díaz, Manuel Neuer , and Alphonso Davies took their turn in the latter.

And PSG's results speak for themselves. Bayern's full-throttle approach last season saw early fireworks and then the slow creep of fatigue later on. It isn't something you can guarantee to avoid, but for sure the Parisians were the fresher and sharper side when the two titans came together in an intense semifinals bout .

Perhaps that is the tricky road for Vincent Kompany and co. to navigate this season: how to rotate without feeling like rotating. Can he pull it off?

articles.title: WXV series about 'turning the page' for Ireland
articles.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says the forthcoming WXV series represents an opportunity to start bringing on new talent with the 2029 World Cup in mind.
articles.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says the upcoming WXV Global Series represents the beginning of a new cycle for his squad leading into the next Women's Rugby World Cup in three years' time.

The Irish team were edged out by France at the quarter-final stage of last year's World Cup and finished third in the 2026 Six Nations, winning all three of their home matches.

Ireland open their WXV Global Series campaign against the United States at Dublin's Tallaght Stadium on Sunday (13:45 BST).

Scott Bemand's side then face Japan in a double-header in Galway and Cork on 27 September and 3 October - the first of which is a WXV game - before WXV games against South Africa in Cape Town on 24 and 31 October.

"We're at the start of a World Cup cycle now. The Six Nations we wanted to keep the momentum from the World Cup going and this is the sort of turning of the page," Bemand told reporters at their Dublin training base.

"Looking three years ahead, what do we need to get under our belts before then?

"We need to develop our depth and see who is coming through. Three years' time there is the potential of something like 28 caps to play for so if you're a new cap coming in now and you go to the World Cup you have the potential of 25-plus caps.

"So we're starting to see talent and understand what talent we need to bring through and this represents the first chance to do that."

Second row Sam Monaghan has been ruled out of the forthcoming fixtures with an achilles injury but Bemand says her absence and that of other injured players opens a door for others to show what they can do.

"It creates the next opportunity for the leader that's already in the group and the next second row to come through," he said.

"We've been developing depth quietly in the background, those girls get an opportunity to train with us and put their hand up for selection and hopefully we'll see a few of those in this series.

"We're starting to build strength on our shores and we have three games coming up now in the global series. We want to have the ability to go deeper in tournaments so you need to build experience."

The Ireland head coach believes his side can improve further in terms of results and performances if they continue to work hard.

"We've got the talent now and the capability to play a couple of different ways but a really good brand of rugby.

"It's exciting, it's fast-paced, it's got power, it's got movement, we're going to be able to kick the ball, we're going to be able to field the ball.

"It feels like we are on the cusp of something. It won't just happen, because each year teams will take us a bit more seriously and those final per cents are always the hardest per cents to come by but the harder we try the better we will get, the luckier we'll get, the bounce of the ball will go the other way.

"The group, the players turn up every day, every week, trying to get better, and it's a pleasure to watch and to be a part of."
authors: Richard Petrie - BBC Sport NI Journalist

articles.title: FA Cup: From depression after serious injury at Chelsea to still playing at 37
articles.summary: Sam Hutchinson is getting ready to play for Farnham Town in the second qualifying round of the FA Cup - 19 years after making his Chelsea debut under Jose Mourinho.
articles.body:
Sam Hutchinson played under both Jose Mourinho and Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea, set up a goal for Frank Lampard, and was in Munich on the historic night they won the Champions League for the first time in 2012.

His time at Chelsea, however, was "filled with regret and what might have been" after a chronic knee injury so nearly ended his career before it had properly started.

A product of Chelsea's youth system, Hutchinson was a promising defender on the fringes of the first team before being diagnosed with a chondral defect (a hole in his right knee) after suffering a serious injury during a reserve game at Aston Villa.

Having joined Chelsea as a seven-year-old, made his first-team debut at 17 under Mourinho and captained England at Under-19s level, Hutchinson took the gut-wrenching decision to retire at the age of 21 in 2010 after struggling to recover.

A period of depression followed for the young player, who had been identified by Mourinho as a bright prospect.

"I had already played for the first team and Mourinho had said some encouraging things about me in interviews," he says.

"Then the injury happened and everything fell apart. I was just a kid.

"After I retired I was in a bad place with dark thoughts."

Hutchinson sought help for his depression.

"Unless you get help, you never know how bad you are," he tells BBC Sport.

"Even telling this story, it's like therapy.

"It's like the old saying - a problem shared is a problem halved. That's true about mental health. If you're suffering in silence, it's not going to help."

After receiving treatment at the Priory, and with his damaged knee finally fixed, Hutchinson came out of retirement in December 2011 to re-sign for Chelsea.

More injuries followed but despite being limited to six senior Chelsea appearances, he has gone on to have a fulfilling career.

Hutchinson played 200-plus games in the Championship, most notably for Sheffield Wednesday, where fans remember him fondly.

In addition to overseas spells in the Netherlands with Vitesse Arnhem and in Cyprus with Pafos, he has also turned out for Nottingham Forest, Reading and AFC Wimbledon.

Sixteen years after fearing his career was over for good, the father-of-three is still playing the game he loves at the age of 37.

This summer Hutchinson signed a two-year contract with non-league Farnham Town - after surviving a major health scare.

Monday, 26 May 2025. A date etched in the memories of AFC Wimbledon fans after their side won promotion to League One by beating Walsall at Wembley in the play-off final.

It was Hutchinson's winner at Grimsby three weeks earlier that ensured the Dons made the play-offs.

He did not know it at the time but the defender-turned-midfielder would not start another game for 11 months after scoring at Blundell Park.

"Throughout the first half my chest was getting increasingly tighter and I was in so much pain," recalls Hutchinson about that game at Grimsby.

"I felt dizzy and my hands started sweating.

"I was rapidly going downhill but then our centre-back won a great header, the keeper tipped it on to the bar, and it dropped down to me to tap over the line."

While AFC Wimbledon's travelling fans celebrated the goal wildly, Hutchinson felt so unwell his only thoughts were finishing the game and making it home to his wife and three children.

It would be several days, however, before he returned to the family home in Ascot.

On the journey back to London, his condition deteriorated to such an extent that a decision was taken to divert the team coach to a hospital in Nottingham so he could receive treatment.

After tests Hutchinson was quickly transferred to a nearby cardiac unit.

"I was put me in the back of an ambulance and I remember hearing the blues and twos," he recalls.

"My blood levels had spiked so much, I was in a really bad way. A couple of the paramedics knew who I was because I had played for Nottingham Forest a few years earlier.

"They said: 'You can thank us later for saving your life.' I was told I'd had a heart attack."

Hutchinson spent the next five days in hospital and had successful heart surgery.

"A branch of an artery was blocked 75%. I had an angiogram , external and had a stent put in by a specialist. The one thing that the professor - who had looked after both Tom Lockyer and Christian Eriksen – said was my situation was nothing like theirs.

"It was a blockage and it was all fixed, there was no need for a defibrillator to be fitted."

John Terry, his former Chelsea team-mate, was among those to reach out to Hutchinson during his recovery, while the player was well enough to visit Wembley to watch AFC Wimbledon win promotion.

A month later the Dons announced he had signed a one-year contract extension after being given the all-clear to train again.

However, Hutchinson was limited to just a handful of appearances in 2025-26 and in May - 12 months after that game at Grimsby - it was announced he would be leaving at the age of 36.

"Sam played a pivotal role in getting us over the line, not only with that iconic goal at Grimsby but his performances leading up to that," said an AFC Wimbledon statement , external announcing his departue.

Some may have decided it was the perfect time to retire from playing after what he had been through.

'I need heart surgery when I stop playing'

It's the opening day of the National League South season and Surrey-based Farnham Town are at home to AFC Totton in their first ever game in the sixth tier of English football.

Three years ago, Farnham struggled to attract crowds of 400 playing in the ninth-tier Combined Counties League.

But three straight promotions, , external together with Hutchinson's arrival in the summer, have caused a stir in the historic market town and there are 1,178 at the 2,200-capacity Memorial Ground to witness his debut, which ends in a 1-0 defeat.

Hutchinson has since gone on to help the part-timers win four of their first eight games and on Saturday will line up for Farnham at Cirencester Town in the second qualifying round of the FA Cup (15:00 BST).

"I'm loving it," he says about playing non-league 19 years after Mourinho sent him on for his Chelsea debut in the 89th minute against Everton on the final day of the 2006-07 Premier League season.

"Part-time football suits me after all that I've been through with my health.

"I have to go back every six months for tests and I have been told I will need further heart surgery when I finally stop playing football.

"But the specialists are happy for me to carry on for now."

It is 16 years since Hutchinson set up a goal for Lampard in Chelsea's 7-0 demolition of Stoke City at Stamford Bridge in 2010; 14 years since he flew to Munich with Roberto di Matteo's squad for the 2012 Champions League final at the Allianz Stadium.

He did not play when the Blues overcame German giants Bayern Munich on penalties to be crowned champions of Europe.

Nevertheless, he was regarded as a valued member of the squad and was invited to the trophy parade that followed.

Despite mixed emotions about his time at Chelsea due to injury, Hutchinson has not forgotten how the club looked after him.

"They brought me up and gave me values," he says. "I look back at the club fondly and what they did for me. I do bits of work now for Chelsea TV."

Hutchinson has also done work to support the British Heart Foundation and raised awareness about mental health.

"I'm in a different place," he says. "I do have regrets [because of the injury] but I have also lived a life that has been good.

"There are many players who have gone through a lot worse than me."

articles.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals Florentino Perez’s role in bringing him to Real Madrid: ‘We stayed in touch for 10 years’
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe’s move to Real Madrid was years in the making, and the Frenchman has now revealed just how important Florentino Perez was in finally making it...
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe 's move to Real Madrid was years in the making, and the Frenchman has now revealed just how important Florentino Perez was in finally making it happen.

In an extensive interview with AS , Mbappe looked back on his journey to the Santiago Bernabeu and explained that there was never really a question over whether he wanted to play for Madrid. The difficult part was making the move possible.

Now in his third season at the club, Mbappe says the reality has matched the dream he had as a child.

Mbappe recalled that his relationship with Perez stretched back a decade before he eventually became a Real Madrid player.

"He's the one who brought me here. We stayed in touch throughout the 10 years leading up to my arrival.

Perez and Mbappe were in touch for 10 years. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"He always showed warmth and understanding regarding every decision made, whether positive or negative for Real Madrid.

"He always told me that one day I'd play for Real Madrid, and here I am – and very happy at that. That's why I have to thank him for everything he's done and continues to do for me. He's the best president in the world."

Those years of contact meant Perez remained a constant figure in Mbappe's path towards Madrid and when the opportunity finally arrived, the forward did not need persuading.

Real Madrid was always Mbappe's destination

Asked whether Real Madrid are what he had imagined as a boy, Mbappe said that playing for Los Blancos had always carried a different significance.

"Yes, absolutely. I was expecting the best club in the world, and to be met with such enthusiasm from Real Madrid fans all over the world.

Mbappe never had any doubts about Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"When I arrived here, I already had a certain status, but when you're a Real Madrid player, you move to another level – a higher level. I think that if you want to be part of football history, you have to play for Real Madrid."

That explains why Mbappe insists nobody actually convinced him to make the move.

"To be honest, nobody and nothing needs to convince you to join Real Madrid.

"Everyone close to me knew that at some point I'd want to join Real Madrid. There was absolutely no doubt that I wanted to come, but sometimes when something isn't possible, there's nothing you can do about it and you have to accept it.

"Nobody had to convince me to come to Real Madrid, not even Florentino Pérez, as great as he is. It was a given," he noted.

articles.title: Alberto Reina no termina de arrancar
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista, una de las revelaciones del Oviedo en Primera, no ha empezado la temporada al nivel esperado
articles.summary: El centrocampista, una de las revelaciones del Oviedo en Primera, no ha empezado la temporada al nivel esperado
articles.body: Alberto Reina fue una de las grandes noticias del Real Oviedo la pasada temporada. En su estreno en Primera División, después de llegar procedente del Mirandés, el centrocampista disputó 37 partidos, 31 como titular, acumuló 2.480 minutos y marcó cuatro goles. Un rendimiento que elevó las expectativas alrededor de un futbolista cuyo futuro también generó incertidumbre durante el verano. El escenario ha cambiado en el inicio de la nueva temporada. Reina ha participado en cuatro de las cinco primeras jornadas, todas ellas como titular, y suma 315 minutos, pero todavía no ha conseguido trasladar al juego la influencia que tuvo durante buena parte del curso anterior. No ha marcado ni asistido y su producción ofensiva está siendo escasa, con un solo disparo en lo que va de campeonato. Los números con balón tampoco esconden un comienzo discreto. El mediocentro suma 142 pases acertados de 170 intentados, un 83,5%, pero todavía no ha encontrado profundidad en su fútbol. El Oviedo espera mucho más de Reina, llamado por condiciones y por lo demostrado la pasada temporada a tener peso en el centro del campo de Julián Calero. El campeonato apenas acaba de comenzar y el margen para cambiar la tendencia es amplio. Después de demostrar en Primera que podía asumir protagonismo en el Oviedo, Reina tiene ahora por delante el reto de recuperar esa versión y volver a convertirse en uno de los futbolistas diferenciales del conjunto azul.

articles.title: El Celta debe recuperar su esencia
articles.standfirst: Más allá de los resultados, el equipo ha perdido su fútbol
articles.summary: Más allá de los resultados, el equipo ha perdido su fútbol
articles.body: El Celta futbolísticamente nada tiene que ver con el de hace dos años y empieza a no parecerse al de hace uno. El primero era un equipo descarado, que buscaba la portería contraria aún sufriendo en la propia. Un conjunto vertical y con una apuesta por un fútbol vistoso. Ese fútbol le devolvió a Europa. La pasada temporada el juego ya mutó pero aún así la clasificación fue mejor y se repitió pase continental. Pero su juego ya era distinto, más sólido en defensa, más resguardado, menos vistosos para el espectador. Previsible en Balaídos, de donde se escaparon 34 puntos en Liga, pero sobresalientes a domicilio. Sin embargo, para el que no siguiese con regularidad al Celta, seguía existiendo la percepción de que era un equipo que mantenía su apuesta por un fútbol de ataque, se dejaban llevar para tal opinión por actuaciones como la del Santiago Bernabéu o eliminatorias europeas. El Celta ya no era hace un año preciosista pero era efectivo, esencialmente como visitante. Independiente de que el arranque de esta temporada sea muy similar en lo numérico al de la pasada y será mejor de vencer este sábado, el actual Celta no es ni el de hace dos años, ni el del pasado. Es un equipo plano, que transmite poco, con posesiones horizontales eternas, que no generan en ataque y al que se le hace de noche en el último tercio del terreno de juego. Un conjunto, futbolísticamente, triste. Todo pasa por recuperar la esencia en su juego, la identidad que les conectó con la grada. No es tarea sencilla. Que ello pueda funcionar dependerá mucho del giro táctico que le pueda dar a su apuesta Claudio Giráldez. El técnico ha mostrado sobradamente su solvencia, lo ha hecho con nota, pero ahora está ante un gran reto y ante un examen importante para él como técnico y por extensión para su equipo, que deberá demostrar su capacidad para plasmarlo.

articles.body: El FC Barcelona de fútbol sala afronta su esperado debut de la temporada en el Palau Blaugrana recibiendo al Servigroup Peñíscola FS en la segunda jornada de la Liga Prime Futsal. El conjunto dirigido por Javi Rodríguez llega a la cita con buenas sensaciones tras imponerse por 2-5 al Viña Albali Valdepeñas en su estreno liguero, en una noche que estará marcada por la celebración previa en la que la plantilla azulgrana ofrecerá a su afición el título de Liga conquistado el pasado curso. articles.standfirst: Carlos Mac Allister, padre y agente del futbolista del Liverpool, asegura que el Liverpool todavía no les ha llamado para renovar y niega cualquier contacto del Real Madrid
articles.summary: Carlos Mac Allister, padre y agente del futbolista del Liverpool, asegura que el Liverpool todavía no les ha llamado para renovar y niega cualquier contacto del Real Madrid
articles.body: El futuro de Alexis Mac Allister comienza a ser uno de los asuntos a resolver en el Liverpool. El centrocampista argentino tiene contrato hasta junio de 2028, pero por el momento no existen conversaciones para prolongar su vinculación con el conjunto de Anfield. Así lo ha reconocido su padre y agente, Carlos Mac Allister, que ha explicado la situación en declaraciones exclusivas a 365Scores Arabia. El mensaje desde el entorno del campeón del mundo es claro. No hay negociación en marcha. “Nadie de la directiva del Liverpool se ha puesto en contacto con nosotros hasta ahora para renovar su contrato”, aseguró Carlos Mac Allister al ser preguntado por la situación de su hijo. Una falta de movimientos que, al menos públicamente, no quieren convertir en un problema con el club. El padre del futbolista insiste en que Alexis tiene todavía contrato y que su obligación pasa por continuar respondiendo sobre el terreno de juego. “Tenemos un contrato vigente y estamos comprometidos con él y con el Liverpool. Si el club no ofrece renovar el contrato, está en su derecho. En este momento, Alexis debe dar lo mejor de sí al club en cada partido”, afirmó. La situación cobra especial importancia después de que el Liverpool haya abordado la renovación de otros futbolistas de la plantilla. Preguntado expresamente por si eso había provocado cierta decepción en Mac Allister, su padre trató de rebajar cualquier posible conflicto, aunque dejó una frase que mantiene abierta la incógnita sobre el futuro. “Alexis no está decepcionado. Es una decisión que toma el club y nosotros no juzgamos sus decisiones. Nos preparamos para lo que pueda venir”, explicó Carlos Mac Allister. Una declaración que refleja la postura que mantiene actualmente el entorno del argentino: respeto absoluto a la decisión del Liverpool, pero también expectación ante los próximos movimientos. Con contrato hasta 2028 y sin una propuesta para ampliarlo encima de la mesa, el paso del tiempo irá ganando peso en la situación del centrocampista. Carlos Mac Allister también fue preguntado por uno de los clubes que ha aparecido relacionado con el futuro del argentino: el Real Madrid. En este caso, su respuesta no dejó margen a interpretaciones. “Nadie del Real Madrid se ha puesto en contacto con nosotros en ningún momento de la carrera de Alexis”, aseguró su padre, descartando así que desde el conjunto blanco se haya producido algún acercamiento al entorno del futbolista. Por ahora, por tanto, el escenario está definido. Mac Allister tiene contrato con el Liverpool hasta 2028, el club no ha iniciado conversaciones para renovarlo y desde su entorno aseguran que tampoco ha existido ningún contacto del Real Madrid. El argentino mantiene su compromiso con los ‘reds’, pero su padre también deja una frase mirando inevitablemente hacia el futuro:“Nos preparamos para lo que pueda venir”

articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer recalled to England squad for Nations League games by Thomas Tuchel
articles.summary: England boss Thomas Tuchel has made eight changes to his squad following the World Cup; Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold returns to the fold along with Chelsea's Cole Palmer; Man City's Phil Foden among the players to miss out
articles.body:
Real Madrid right-back Alexander-Arnold returns to the fold for the first time since June 2025 along with Chelsea's Palmer, who was another high-profile World Cup omission.

Tuchel has made eight changes from the World Cup in his 27-man group for the three-week camp, during which England, third-place finishers in the summer, will play four Nations League fixtures against Spain, Croatia and Czech Republic.

Liverpool's 18-year-old winger Rio Nguhoma , who impressed in England's World Cup warm-up fixtures, has also been called up along with uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott .

Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite receives his first call-up since Tuchel's appointment, while there are also recalls for Lewis Hall , Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Myles Lewis-Skelly .

Phil Foden is once again overlooked by Tuchel along with Morgan Gibbs-White and Adam Wharton , while World Cup squad members Ollie Watkins , Ivan Toney and Noni Madueke drop out.

Reece James, John Stones , Djed Spence , Dan Burn , Jordan Henderson, Ben White and Dean Henderson are absent with injuries.

Manchester United's Kobbie Mainoo is included despite being an unused member of the World Cup squad.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion), James Trafford (Leeds United) Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trevoh Chalobah (Como), Marc Guéhi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Tino Livramento (Newcastle United), Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen) Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Alex Scott (AFC Bournemouth) Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Marcus Rashford (Manchester United), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea), Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)

Tuchel: Palmer and Trent must fight for places

Asked about Alexander-Arnold and Palmer's recalls, Tuchel said: "They had a good start to the season. They never did something wrong, we just chose different players. Now is a new competition.

"Cole has his numbers back. Assists, decisive goals. I think he has a point to prove.

"The same goes for Trent. He was never non-selectable. Now is his chance to show, to come to camp and be the best version of himself. He comes as a right-back for us.

"He needs to perform; it's a competition. He was not with us at the World Cup; we trusted other players, and I stick with that decision.

"It's now time to fight for his place. He always said he's up for the fight. It's now up to him to prove. We have a long camp and I'm sure he'll show up."

Is this a better squad than the World Cup?

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

Tuchel has learnt from his mistakes in the summer with his World Cup squad because he has made a lot of changes with this squad.

As far as I'm concerned, Tuchel is still on the naughty step. I still haven't forgiven him for what happened against Argentina. He still has it all to prove.

But by looking at this squad, I think he is admitting he made some mistakes.

This is a better and more balanced squad than he took to the World Cup.

'Trent call-up a massive shift from Tuchel'

It shouldn't be a shock to see an Englishman playing for Real Madrid selected in the England squad but Alexander-Arnold's selection is exactly that.

This marks a massive shift from Tuchel, who previously said Alexander-Arnold was not the profile of right-back he wanted in his side and repeatedly declined to select the former Liverpool star - even when Tino Livramento suffered a pre-World Cup injury and Tuchel had the opportunity to call up a replacement.

Questions over why Tuchel overlooked the technically gifted 27-year-old resurfaced when the England boss questioned the natural ability of Three Lions players to retain possession and control games under pressure.

Alexander-Arnold hadn't been in an England squad since the summer of 2025 so what's changed?

His performances for Real Madrid this season didn't move the needle alone.

He has one assist from five appearances and his deployment in midfield for the Champions League win over Inter Milan was a reminder of the continuing conundrum managers are having in getting the most out of Alexander-Arnold's potential.

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho used Alexander-Arnold in central midfield due to injuries and applauded his application - but also noted how he lost possession and the physical challenges of the role.

Last season, Alexander-Arnold was battling Dani Carvajal for the right-back spot at Real Madrid. This season, it's summer signing Denzel Dumfries competing with him for the place.

The brilliant on-the-ball ability remains, but defensive concerns persist. How Tuchel uses Alexander-Arnold - and what this change of stance means in the longer term - will be an intriguing narrative throughout the international break.

Saturday September 26: Spain (H), kick-off 7.45pm

Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pm

Saturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pm

Tuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm

Your views: 'This is the squad he should have picked for the World Cup'

JoeR: I am slightly confused. If Tuchel thought Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold weren't good enough for the World Cup squad, has much really changed in the first few games of the season? This is basically Tuchel admitting he got the World Cup selection wrong.

Lincpoacher: It's about time that Alexander-Arnold was back in the team with his outstanding long passing that can open tight defences; it's what we needed for a long time!

Fenners: Quite like the look of that squad. It will be interesting to see if Scott and Tino Livramento get many minutes. Still a little concerned about the back-line, though.

Micky045: The squad he's now picked is the one that should've gone to the World Cup. So many names left out this time shouldn't have been anywhere near that squad. Similarly, some of the names picked this time round should have.

Luke: Happy to see Branthwaite back in the set-up. Been immense for Everton so far this season.

articles.title: Dom Hyam: Wrexham defender's Scotland disappointment
articles.summary: Wrexham defender Dom Hyam reveals his disappointment at being left out of Scotland's Nations League squad and says he is yet to speak to new national team boss Sebastien Pocognoli.
articles.body:
Dom Hyam hopes he can work his way back into the Scotland set-up in future amid his disappointment at being omitted from new boss Sebastien Pocognoli's first international squad.

Belgian Pocognoli, 39, signed a two-year contract with Scotland in August following the departure of Steve Clarke after the 2026 World Cup.

Hyam was included in Clarke's squad for the summer showpiece, although he was an unused substitute for the Scots' group stage matches against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil.

The Wrexham defender was left out of Pocognoli's 28-man squad for Scotland's opening block of Nations League fixtures - which include a double header with Slovenia along with matches against Switzerland and North Macedonia.

"It is a little bit tough. There's a bit of change in the set-up with the new manager," said Hyam, who has won four senior Scotland caps.

"But my immediate reaction was disappointment, I can't lie. Hopefully there'll be more opportunities to come in the future.

"Like I've said all along, it's all about how I perform on the pitch for my club and hopefully I can get in in the future."

When asked if he has spoken to Pocognoli since the former Belgium left-back was appointed as boss just over a month ago, Hyam responded: "Not with the new manager personally, no.

"But I'm still open and I've just got to focus on myself."

Wrexham owners aim Spygate dig at Southampton

Parkinson's 'wriggle room' as Wrexham seek response

Captain Hyam has featured in each of Wrexham's eight matches across all competitions so far this season.

As a key member of the Championship club's leadership group, Hyam revealed manager Phil Parkinson spoke to both him and midfielder Matty James in the aftermath of the Red Dragons' emphatic 6-0 loss to West Ham United .

The defeat was the biggest of Parkinson's tenure since he was appointed as Wrexham manager in the summer of 2021.

It was also the club's heaviest league defeat since losing to Bournemouth by the same scoreline 22 years ago.

But Hyam felt it was important to hold talks with Parkinson as Wrexham seek to respond in a positive manner when they host Southampton at the Racecourse Ground on Saturday (15:00 BST).

"He (Parkinson) spoke to myself and Matty James after the game," Hyam said.

"He just wanted our opinions on how we move forward from the last game and into the next one.

"I felt it was very important that we addressed it, but we've quickly drawn a line underneath it.

"We spoke about what we didn't do so well, and then all the focus was clearly next on Southampton .

"I'm sure there'll be another few times in my career where there'll be a terrible scoreline, but that's just the way football goes. It's just about how we react."

Wrexham currently sit 19th having collected seven of the 21 points on offer so far this season.

Southampton are ninth with 10 points, despite being docked four points prior to the campaign as a result of the Spygate scandal .

articles.title: ESPN College GameDay 2026 TV Schedule, Predictions and Location for Week 3
articles.summary: ESPN's College GameDay regularly presents the marquee matchups of college football, though the highlight games themselves have been a big of a mixed bag in 2026.
articles.body:
ESPN's College GameDay regularly presents the marquee matchups of college football, though the highlight games themselves have been a big of a mixed bag in 2026.

Last week's thriller between the Ohio State Buckeyes and Texas Longhorns was one of the best games of the year to date and was a potential playoff preview. The Week 1 "battle" between LSU and Clemson, on the other hand, yielded a 51-10 blowout LSU victory.

LSU will be back in the spotlight this week with a game that should be much more competitive. The seventh-ranked Tigers are set to visit No. 9 Mississippi in a game that features storylines galore.

Here's a look at what you need to know about the game and the College GameDay broadcast.

Location: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi

TV and Live Stream: ESPN, ESPNU, ESPN app

Line and Over/Under: LSU -2.5, 57.5 total points

Saturday night's matchup between LSU and Mississippi is big for a couple of different reasons. For starters, it's a battle between SEC contenders and College Football Playoff (CFP) hopefuls.

LSU and Mississippi are ranked seventh and ninth, respectively, in the coaches poll .

Of course, the bigger storyline is the fact that the game marks Lane Kiffin's highly anticipated return to Oxford. Kiffin left Mississippi before last year's CFB to take the head-coaching gig at LSU. Players like Princewill Umanmielen and assistants like Charlie Weis Jr. soon followed.

While Kiffin has embraced the role of college football's villain since making the jump, not every Ole Miss player is holding a grudge.

"Still my guy. Just a great head coach, can't hold it against him. We're all still cool," receiver Deuce Alexander said, per Sam Hutchins of the Clarion Ledger .

You can bet, though, that the fans will be ready to give Kiffin an unpleasant homecoming. Much of the game will hinge on how the Tigers deal with the rowdy Mississippi crowd.

On paper, LSU appears well positioned to get the road win. It features a dominant pass rush that can pressure Trinidad Chambliss early and often, and it has enough speed at receiver to constantly threaten a suspect Rebels secondary. Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt is a top-tier signal-caller in his own right and should be able to handle the hostile environment.

Of course, Mississippi has Chambliss, college football's magic man and arguably the top quarterback playing in 2026. The prediction here is that LSU commands the action early, but Chambliss leads a late surge for a miracle come-from-behind victory.

It'll be a close one, and we may well see a rematch during the playoff, but Chambliss and the Rebels faithful could be too much for Kiffin to overcome.

articles.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel recalls Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer with warning
articles.summary: England boss Thomas Tuchel recalls Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer but says players have to "perform".
articles.body:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel says "the door is always open" after recalling Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer to his first squad since the World Cup - but has warned players they have to "perform".

Tuchel controversially left Real Madrid right-back Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Palmer out of his squad for the summer tournament in North America.

Both return for four Nations League games during an extended international break after this weekend's club fixtures.

Alexander-Arnold, 27, won the most recent of his 34 England caps when he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 win against Andorra in June 2025.

He has made five appearances, including three starts, for Real Madrid so far this season, registering one assist.

Palmer, 24, last played for England in a 1-0 friendly defeat by Japan in March. He has scored four goals and provided two assists in six games this season.

"They had a good start to the season," said Tuchel, who has again omitted Manchester City's Phil Foden. "They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad.

"I think he has a point to prove, and the same goes for Trent. He was never off the list. He was never non-selectable for us, and it is his chance to show, come to camp and be the best version of himself."

Alexander-Arnold played in midfield in Real's Champions League win over Inter Milan earlier this month, but Tuchel said he had picked the former Liverpool player as a full-back.

"He had a good start in two positions for Real Madrid and he comes as a right-back for us," he said.

On his trust in Alexander Arnold, Tuchel said: "[He needs to] perform, that's just what it is. It is a competition and I understand the question because he was not with us at the World Cup. We trusted other players.

"I still stick with this decision and it is now time to fight for his place. He always said he is up for a fight, he always said he is up to fight for his place - especially for England - so it is on him to prove and he is more than welcome in camp.

"We have a long camp and I am sure he will show up."

Tuchel said the onus was now on players to impress in the international set-up.

"It is one thing to be nominated, like with Cole, and getting your ticket back in the squad but it's another thing to perform for England," he said.

"Cole needs to step up when he comes and he needs to show these kind of numbers to get his place, keep his shirt and justify the nomination."

Giving a message to his players, he later told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Jordan Henderson said it so professionally well before the match against France - you just never know when your next England match is coming.

"So, guys, this is it - this is the next England match you play to the fullest, you show up with the right attitude, and you give it your all, because you never know.

"It is not even a shout-out to Trent; it is a shout-out to everyone. It's the mentality that we want to have.

"If you come to camp it is not an international break, it's an international window."

England host World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September, then travel to Czech Republic (Tuesday, 29 September) and Croatia (Saturday, 3 October) before the Czechs visit on Tuesday, 6 October.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha, who were both in the Three Lions' pre-World Cup squad, both feature again.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin, whose three top-flight goals so far this season have helped Leeds United go third in the Premier League, is also included.

Tuchel has also picked Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall, Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite, Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play at left-back or in midfield, and Brighton keeper Jason Steele.

Dean Henderson, Jordan Henderson, Reece James, Djed Spence and John Stones, who were all in the World Cup squad, miss out, with Tuchel saying they were not selected because of injuries.

Along with Foden, other notable absentees are Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White, Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton and Manchester United's Harry Maguire.

Tuchel regrets not eating Azteca turf after win over Mexico

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton), James Trafford (Leeds United)

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trevoh Chalobah (Como), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Tino Livramento (Newcastle United), Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen)

Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Alex Scott (Bournemouth)

Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Marcus Rashford (Manchester United), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea), Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)

The Nations League matches will be England's first since the 2026 World Cup, where they were beaten in the semi-finals by Argentina.

The Three Lions took a 1-0 lead but conceded two late goals, with former England captain Wayne Rooney saying the team "crumbled" and became "too passive", which he said started from "the manager and the decisions he made".

Though England missed out on their first men's World Cup final in 60 years, they beat France 6-4, having led 4-0 at half-time, in an thrilling bronze-medal match.

"The more I reflect on it, it's maybe more buying into our strengths and playing more minutes like we played in the second half against Croatia and the first half against France," said Tuchel.

"Buying into these strengths because we get a lot of value out of it. We get a lot of connection to the fans. This is what the Premier League reflects.

"Football is about adapting to situations, and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach if you look at the 6-4 against France - but people talk about it like it's one of their most nicest experiences ever.

"Maybe I have to compromise in my wish and urge for control - for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best [in us].

"We will adjust our style but always to put the strengths of the players as the first priority."

Tuchel's defensive substitutions were called into question following the defeat by Argentina, but he played down how much of an issue that was with England supporters.

"I tell you something, 99.9% of the fans don't speak about substitutions and tactical things," he said.

"They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second-half energy of the Croatia match. They speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against DR Congo and where they celebrated.

"This is the feedback that I get. This is what we created and how it should be.

"This is what a World Cup is for, to connect with people and give them experiences that they do not forget. It makes me proud."

The Football Association has conducted what Tuchel described as a "sometimes painful, sometimes emotional" review into England's World Cup campaign.

Tuchel said he felt "support from all my bosses" at the tournament and "there was never a doubt in my mind or their mind that we will continue together".

Among the highlights of the Three Lions' tournament was a 3-2 defeat of co-hosts Mexico at the Azteca Stadium, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men following Jarell Quansah's red card.

"It was a very special moment before the Mexico game, where we had a talk and my bosses told me we know anything can happen in a football game, and in Mexico," said Tuchel.

"'Don't worry, we see what is going on and we want to continue like this.' It is a beautiful moment for me as a coach."

Since the World Cup, Fifa president Gianni Infantino has come under increasing pressure following a failed plan to sell off stakes in competitions to private investors, and for the manner in which United States forward Folarin Balogun had a suspension overturned.

Balogun was sent off during his side's win against Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last 32 but was allowed to play against Belgium in the last 16 when he would have expected to be serving a one-match suspension.

That came after US President Donald Trump asked Fifa to review it.

The FA has withdrawn its support for Infantino's re-election and asked him to release all documents relating to both controversies.

"I told you how I am backed from my bosses so the minimum I can do is back my bosses," said Tuchel.

"They have my full support on that and back their opinion. I'm grateful that I can talk about football, that's my little bit of knowledge that I have and not about sport politics."

articles.title: El baño de masas de Florentino: "Toda Ceuta estaba aquí"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Real Madrid visitó la ciudad ceutí junto al presidente de honor, José Martínez 'Pirri', y al director de Relaciones Institucionales, Emilio Butragueño.
articles.summary: El presidente del Real Madrid visitó la ciudad ceutí junto al presidente de honor, José Martínez 'Pirri', y al director de Relaciones Institucionales, Emilio Butragueño.
articles.body: A eso de las 11:20 aterrizaba Florentino Pérez en Ceuta, junto al presidente de honor, José Martínez 'Pirri', y al director de Relaciones Institucionales, Emilio Butragueño. Allí, en el mismo helipuerto, le esperaba ya el presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta, Juan Vivas. La bienvenida ha sido acompañada de un caluroso abrazo y de una breve charla en la que el presidente del Real Madrid ha denominado a Vivas como "el ceutí más ilustre". El baño de masas del máximo dirigente del club blanco ha empezado desde ese momento, con los trabajadores del helipuerto y aficionados que esperaban en la terminal. De allí se han ido al Palacio Autonómico donde aguardaba una inmensa cantidad de seguidores del club capitalino y de su presidente. Florentino ha bajado del coche entre vítores, cánticos y aplausos, al más puro estilo 'estrella de rock'. El acto dentro del ayuntamiento ha constado de dos partes. Primero ha tenido lugar la firma en el Libro de Honor de la Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta. Tanto Florentino Pérez, presidente del Real Madrid, como Pirri, presidente de honor y caballa de nacimiento, han estampado su firma, junto a una breve dedicatoria que han leído a cámara. A continuación, los protagonistas han acudido al Salón del Trono del Ayuntamiento, donde han dado un breve discurso para los allí presentes. El primero en tomar la palabra ha sido Juan Vivas. El presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta ha querido dar las gracias al Real Madrid por su visita y por el gesto que ha tenido con la ciudad. Le ha tomado la palabra Pirri, quién ha rememorado sus orígenes por las calles que lo han visto crecer, antes de acabar con un "viva Ceuta y su gente". El último en hablar ha sido Florentino Pérez, quien ha querido desligar la visita a Ceuta con la polémica reciente con las camisetas de apoyo a la población ceutí. Al finalizar, el Salón ha estallado en una enorme ovación. Ha sido entonces cuando ha llegado el turno de obsequios, y, especialmente, de fotos. El presidente blanco ha estado más de media hora haciéndose fotos con todos los allí presentes. Ha firmado autógrafos, ha charlado con los miembros de la peña madridista de la ciudad, e incluso ha tenido tiempo para alguna broma y carantoña. Antes de irse, ha hablado en exclusiva para MARCA, donde ha asegurado, de forma irónica, que parecía que "toda Ceuta estaba aquí" y que "la gente está sufriendo bastante".

articles.title: Spain reveal Nations League squad in Ceuta in support of migration crisis
articles.summary: World Cup winners Spain choose Ceuta to announce Nations League squad in solidarity with border crossing troubles.
articles.body:
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente announced his Nations League squad from Ceuta on Friday in a show of support for the Spanish city in northern Africa that has become the centre of a migration crisis.

For his first squad announcement since Spain won the World Cup in July, De la Fuente revealed his list in a video featuring him in Ceuta accompanied by residents of the Spanish exclave. More than 70,000 people stormed across the border in late July from Morocco, with more than 100 dying in the chaos. Most quickly returned, but a few thousand remain in the city of just over 80,000.

De la Fuente did not directly mention the border crossing or its impact, but did say: “This is Ceuta, this is Spain.” It echoed the rise in sentiment in Spain that Ceuta – a territory that until the mass crossing was mostly an afterthought for most mainland Spaniards – needs to be supported.

Spain opens the Nations League against England at Wembley Stadium on September 26 , when its players will wear two stars on their shirts for the first time since winning their second world title.

After visiting London, Spain will host Croatia on September 29 and the Czech Republic on October 3 , before visiting Croatia on October 6 .

De la Fuente kept his World Cup squad mostly intact.

Inter Milan goalkeeper Josep Martinez replaces Barcelona’s Joan Garcia, who is out with a minor knee issue. Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen is in for Marcos Llorente, who retired from international football. Fermin Lopez replaces fellow Barcelona midfielder Gavi, while Espanyol striker Roberto Fernandez got his first call-up, replacing Borja Iglesias.

Ceuta is one of two Spanish territories on the north African coast along with Melilla. Ceuta has been in Spanish possession since 1580. Christians and Muslims, Spanish and Moroccan residents and day workers all live there in relative harmony behind a border fence that many migrants from across Africa attempt to cross or swim around for a better life in Europe.

A Real Madrid supporters’ group has demanded a public apology from their star striker Kylian Mbappe and two of his teammates after the trio declined to fully wear a T-shirt in support of the people of Ceuta.

articles.title: England squad: Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions selections analysed as Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer return after World Cup
articles.summary: Cole Palmer, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Morgan Gibbs-White, Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden feature among our England squad talking points after Thomas Tuchel made eight changes from the group he took to the World Cup for the upcoming Nations League games
articles.body:
Cole Palmer's form at the start of this season for Chelsea has been irresistible. Four goals and two assists in six games, and his link-up play with England team-mate Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro has been sensational to watch.

"Cole has his numbers back," said Thomas Tuchel at his press conference. "Assists, decisive goals. I think he has a point to prove."

The England boss really had no choice but to recall him after leaving Palmer out of his World Cup squad.

The omission may have ultimately helped Palmer, who was hit by injury and looked a shadow of himself last season following the previous summer's Club World Cup. Rested, refreshed and back towards his best.

Could even a below-par Palmer have helped England in North America? There will be many that will argue his case.

But the question now is how and where does Tuchel use Palmer going forwards?

Jude Bellingham locked down the No 10 role at the World Cup. The Real Madrid ace was one of the tournament's stars. Meanwhile, Bukayo Saka is back fit and firing for Arsenal on the right. Anthony Gordon is excelling at Barcelona on the left wing after impressing there for England in the summer.

Rogers, too, has been a key figure for Tuchel. Finding a way to get the two Chelsea attackers together on the pitch will be an exciting challenge for the England boss, who has an abundance of attacking options. Peter Smith

Kobbie Mainoo's inclusion comes after he was the only outfield player not to play a single minute during England's World Cup campaign. This time, Tuchel promises it will be different for the Manchester United midfielder, who has started the season strongly.

"I expect him to be on the pitch and it's my duty to get him on the pitch," said the England boss. "That was totally on me. He didn't put a foot wrong during the World Cup.

"He was class in behaviour on the training pitch. There was big competition; we played Reece (James) in central midfield also. Elliot Anderson is amazing for us; Declan Rice is a very unique player.

"We trusted them more than we trusted Kobbie. It was difficult for him. It was on me."

The competition for places in England's midfield remains fierce. But clearly Mainoo is a part of Tuchel's plans and there are no hard feelings. The nature of the camp, spanning three weeks and including four fixtures, should allow him chances to prove his worth. Nick Wright

It should not be a shock to see an Englishman playing for Real Madrid selected in the England squad but Trent Alexander-Arnold's selection is exactly that.

This marks a massive shift from Tuchel, who previously said Alexander-Arnold was not the profile of right-back he wanted in his side and repeatedly declined to select the former Liverpool star - even when Tino Livramento suffered a pre-World Cup injury and Tuchel had the opportunity to call up a replacement.

Questions over why Tuchel overlooked the technical 27-year-old reoccurred when the England boss questioned the natural ability of Three Lions players to be able to retain the ball and control games under pressure.

Alexander-Arnold had not been in an England squad since the summer of 2025 so what has changed?

"He was never non-selectable," said Tuchel when asked about Alexander-Arnold. "Now is his chance to show, come to camp, be the best version of himself. He comes as a right-back for us."

His performances for Real Madrid this season did not shift the needle alone.

He has one assist from five appearances and his deployment in midfield for the Champions League win over Inter Milan was a reminder of the continuing conundrum managers are having in getting the most out of Alexander-Arnold's potential.

Real boss Jose Mourinho used Alexander-Arnold in central midfield due to injuries and applauded his application - but also noted how he had lost possession and noted the physical challenge of the role.

Last season, Alexander-Arnold was battling with Dani Carvajal for the right-back spot at Real Madrid. This season it is summer signing Denzel Dumfries challenging him for the place.

The brilliant on-the-ball ability remains but defensive concerns continue. How Tuchel uses Alexander-Arnold - and what this change of stance means longer term - will be an intriguing narrative through the international break. Peter Smith

If England cannot control games, why not 'embrace the chaos'?

Tuchel was critical of England's 'DNA' after the loss to Argentina, suggesting the players were unable to control high-pressure matches with possession in the way a team like Spain can.

The return of technical players Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to his squad seemed to be an admission he had left some of the best English players at looking after the ball out of the group. But in his press conference on Friday Tuchel hinted that perhaps it is better for England to go the other way - and "embrace the chaos".

"The more I reflect on it [the Argentina loss], it's more buying into our strengths and playing more like in the second half against Croatia, or first half against France," said Tuchel. "We get a lot of value out of it [this style]. This is what the Premier League reflects.

"Football is about adapting to situations, and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach. If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it's one of their nicest experiences ever to watch a football match.

"Maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control - maybe we need more chaos, to embrace the chaos. Maybe it brings out the best.

"We will adjust our style but always to put the strengths of the players on the first priority." Peter Smith

Morgan Gibbs-White can feel justifiably aggrieved by his omission. The 26-year-old was outstanding last season for Nottingham Forest, racking up 15 Premier League goals and registering four assists. He has continued in the same vein this term.

Gibbs-White continues to face intense competition for places in the No 10 position. Palmer has been recalled to a squad which already features Bellingham, Rogers and Eberechi Eze. Tuchel says the numbers do not add up.

"He was close but it's always the same," he said. "It makes no sense to choose three, four or five No 10s. It just doesn't help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan is in. He ended the season strongly and was the key player for Forest to not be relegated."

Gibbs-White might wonder why Eze was preferred. The Arsenal man has not started a Premier League game this season and produced roughly half as many Premier League goal involvements as Gibbs-White last term. But all Gibbs-White can do is keep pushing, and be ready if the recalled Palmer does not deliver.

"It's one thing to be chosen, like Cole, and get your ticket back to the squad, but it's another thing to perform for England," added Tuchel. "Cole, especially, needs to step up when he comes and show these kinds of numbers and performances to get his place, keep his shirt and justify the nomination." Nick Wright

Gibbs-White is not the only No 10 to have been crowded out. Phil Foden is also on the outside looking in having been overlooked for Tuchel's World Cup squad too.

The Manchester City star was included in Tuchel's squads in March of this year and November of 2025, but this omission comes after an encouraging start to the season was interrupted by his red card in last weekend's Manchester derby.

Foden now faces an almighty battle, in an area of the pitch in which England are well stocked, to win Tuchel over and earn a place back in his plans. His latest omission, as Tuchel returns to other technicians such as Alexander-Arnold, will feel painful. Nick Wright

Is Tuchel embracing England's next generation?

The England manager has pivoted from the experienced squad he selected for the World Cup and made a marked effort to give chances to a plethora of young talent in his latest camp.

Veteran England presences like Jordan Henderson, Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins have been omitted, leaving room for the inclusion of Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha - all of whom are under the age of 23, with the latter having turned 18 less than a month ago.

Ngumoha's inclusion is without doubt the most eye-catching.

The teenage sensation travelled with England's squad to Florida for their pre-tournament training camp and has appeared in five of Liverpool's six games to start the season, impressing enough to be called up even without recording a goal contribution thus far this campaign.

Perhaps easier choices were that of Lewis-Skelly and Scott in the midfield. The former has excelled for unbeaten league leaders Arsenal, recording two assists from deep-lying midfield and keeping £75m summer signing Bruno Guimaraes out of the champions' starting line-up.

Scott has continued to build on an impressive 2025/26 campaign in which he represented arguably the key component in a Bournemouth side that qualified for European football for the first time. Those performances - alongside earning him his place - meant he was linked to high-profile suitors like Chelsea and Manchester United throughout the summer.

"We had three players in prep camp with us [before the World Cup], Alex Scott, Rio Ngumoha and Josh [King], all three of them were fantastic members of the squad," Tuchel said.

"Not only because they were nice and reliable and excellent characters, but they showed the quality, courage and curiosity on the pitch, which was very nice to see."

Whether Tuchel ushers in new tactics remains to be seen - but his first England squad since the World Cup has shown a willingness to at least include new players. Noah Langford
